## Loot Goblins V13.4: identity, journey, and current scope

Loot Goblins is a social possession-and-escape game: steal ridiculous treasure from dangerous islands and other players, then somehow get it home. The desired rhythm is explore with awe, take something valuable, feel the world react, improvise an escape, bank the reward, and choose another risk. Fast movement and boat handling should be enjoyable before a reward appears. Danger challenges that power rather than restoring difficulty by making ordinary travel sluggish.

This guide describes **V13.4 (The Living Port, polished)**, on branch `feature/v13-4-port-polish` (a PR stacked on V13.3's branch, not merged), which polishes **V13.3 (The Living Port)** on branch `feature/v13-3-living-port` (PR #28 to main, not merged), on top of the **V13.2 (Sea of Chaos)** code on main. **V13.4 answers Ninety's brief to make V13.3's content feel finished and to put raid competition at the centre of the Port**: a weekly PIRATE CHAMPIONSHIP beside the Biggest Haul and the monthly PIRATE LEGENDS (V13.3's monthly board, renamed, its data kept), all three in a rebuilt Hall of Legends behind the podium with past champions, places that show at once, prizes on every board, a 🏆 chip and LEGENDS page, and raid-board places on the after-raid card; every Port game gets START NOW, the score to beat, splits, retry on `R` and a results card that says how close it came, plus a Regatta rocket start, Gauntlet shortcuts, a Derby with perfect timing, streaks and a commentator, range streaks and a crab counter; a colour-coded signpost and venue flags; CLAIM ALL and a claim pop; clearer challenges; pets that greet you. See **V13.4: The Living Port, polished** below and docs/reports/2026-10-23-v13-4-port-polish.md. **Nobody has played V13.4 either**: it was validated by lint, builds and 140 Luau tests. **V13.3 answers Ninety's brief to give goblins reasons to play another raid and another day**: seven Port games on one framework (the Tiny Boat Regatta, the Grapple Gauntlet, Cannon Golf, the Pet Derby, Treasure Toss, the Target Ship Gallery and Crab Chaos), the Captain's Quest Board (three daily and three weekly quests), weekly and monthly leaderboards with tier and placement rewards in a Hall of Records, a floating pet sanctuary for every goblin with pet expeditions, challenges between goblins, a what's-next card after every raid, titles, and retention analytics; all paid in capped Shinies. See **V13.3: The Living Port** below and docs/reports/2026-10-22-v13-3-living-port.md. **Nobody has played V13.3**: it was validated by lint, builds and 136 automated Luau tests, as the brief asked. V13.2 came through PR #24 (V13, the Goblin Port), PR #25 (V13.1, the playtest fixes) and PR #26 (V13.2, Sea of Chaos), all merged on 2026-10-22, after V11 and V12 merged in PRs #22 and #23. **V13.2 answers Ninety's brief to make encounters more frequent, movement more expressive, boats more balanced and every raid unpredictable**: running builds momentum by itself (no sprint key) and the grapple swings; the fleet shares one speed band (106 to 118) and grows to ten with the Anchorjack, the Wavebreaker and the Corsair; every boat has a bow gun on the click; the skyship flies a route with finite cannon reach and a countdown the server enforces; going on a raid is a choice made in the Port; and every raid has one of eight world-chaos events. ### The first raid from a player's perspective

The world generates when Play starts, taking several seconds on the reported development machine; players are loaded after world construction. **Since V13 a goblin arrives in the Goblin Port** (a harbour town on its own island far to the south) and spends the minute between raids there: the Shipyard, the pet menagerie, the wardrobe, the Spyglass (watch the raid) and the podium; **since V13.2 going is a choice**: JOIN NEXT RAID, or walking up the gangplank onto the little airship, signs a goblin up, and when the countdown ends only those signed up go to the skyship (with nobody signed up there is no countdown and no raid). **A raid begins aboard the skyship** (V7): a flying pirate ship 540 studs up. Since V13.2 it waits at one end of one of seven routes for 10 s while goblins aim (the cannons locked), then crosses the sea in 32 s; a cannon throws about 1,200 studs, so the islands in reach change as it flies. Goblins climb into a cannon and aim it by looking at where they want to land (V8), are thrown on a plain arc and tumble with loose limbs, and come down on land (head first like an ostrich if they fall fast, on their feet if they brake with a glide) or on the sea (which skips a fast goblin up to three times, each bounce smaller). They can also walk out along the ship's wings and step off. Since V12 an island picked on the map (`M`) is a promise: the cannon starts aimed at that island's **landing spot** (dry, open ground near its treasure, on the side facing the ship, under a beam), and a goblin still aboard when the window closes is fired there (V13.2: the map lights the islands in reach on this route, and a pick is fired at as the ship passes it). A line along the bottom of the screen always says what to do next and which key does it. Goblin Cove is home. The Hoard is the visible gold ring/beam where treasure and coin proceeds are banked; it is never on the ship. Home also has boats, keg access, a practice cannon, movement toys, and a harbor jump. The intended introductory line is the harbor jump, the teal Gate Run, and the passage through the reef to the Crossroads. Home Bay deliberately leaves calm water and visual breathing room.

The near islands offer inexpensive short trips. Middle destinations add longer journeys and characteristic trouble. Far islands have harder return routes. Values are flat (4 to 11 gold) except the **Golden Idol (17)**, the prize of the sea. A treasure's light pillar, the map (M), the compass and the minimap help choose a destination; since V9 no names or values float on the horizon (they show only up close). Since V9 whatever guards a treasure **follows the thief across the sea almost to Goblin Cove**, ending at the sanctuary's gold lantern buoys. The physical geography gives currents, reef passes, ramps, cover, high ground, and alternate routes that influence pursuit. A thief normally carries one treasure at a time. The personal decision is which treasure is worth exposing oneself for, and how to return without being robbed or stopped by the world.

A raid is **six minutes** of play (`Config.RAID_DURATION` 360, V9); since V13 the time between raids is the Goblin Port's 60 s countdown (V13.2: it starts with the first sign-up, and is shortened to 8 s when everyone signed up has walked aboard), not V9's 10 s on the skyship. The raid opens with a 42 s launch window (V13.2: 10 s of prep with the cannons locked, then the 32 s pass; through V13.1 it was 20 s standing still) and **the six-minute clock starts when the window closes**, so a goblin who fires late still gets the whole six minutes; anyone still aboard when the pass ends is fired off at their pick if it is in reach, else at the best landing in reach. A goblin can leave a running raid (LEAVE THIS RAID on the `H` card, two presses): home to the Port, dropping what they carry and losing that raid's gold and Shinies. In the last 50 s banking pays 25% more (the final rush). Banking adds Gold for that raid. At its end, every player tied for the highest positive Gold receives a Win; a zero-score raid has no winner. Gold resets next raid, and the world resets its systems. Wins are session values, not saved progression. Loose or carried treasure not banked in time does not become score. **Since V13.1 nobody dies**: a goblin whose health runs out is knocked out for 5 s where they fell, drops what they carry (loose, for anyone), and gets up with full health; only a body that falls out of the world, or the Reset button, is respawned. No creature takes treasure from a goblin's hands: their hits hurt a carrier until a knockout drops it.

Taking treasure triggers its own trouble and adds shared Heat. Continuing to carry outside the home ward raises Heat; when nobody carries, Heat cools. Other players and world threats create exposure. The intended social result is improvised chases, theft, escape, group reactions, and another raid. Existing solo mechanical observations and some human feedback do not establish full multiplayer fun or fairness.

### Player verbs and tradeoffs

Run (building momentum), dash, air-jump, grapple and swing, board, steer, brake, drift, boost, fire the bow gun, play the boat's ability, steal, throw, swing a sword, light a beacon, raise a chain, launch a keg, fire a cannon, hide, and bank. Not every verb needs a new system. The shared E key favors an actual visible prompt over spirit casting; `Shift` or `C` dash on foot; `C` drifts while driving (V13.2).

Running is free and, since V13.2, builds by itself from 21 to 38 over about two seconds (momentum; there is no sprint). Stamina pays for the exceptional moves (dash, air jump, a carrier's sword); carrying treasure increases their costs and slightly slows the carrier. A carrier can defend themselves with a weaker, slower, shorter, tiring sword swing, and can grapple to surfaces/boats but cannot use the grapple to steal another treasure. Boats trade speed, durability, draft, handling, capacity, and cannon access. Geography can separate a shallow-water player route from a deep-draft Navy route. A beacon diverts nearby Navy, and the fort chain prevents new departures from its harbor for a period.

The score remains treasure. Coins encourage taking a skillful or interesting route, repair a little hull, and refund some boost cooldown; ten convert to one Gold when banked, with at most six Gold from coins in a raid. Timed courses provide a different movement challenge and a local best-time sign. Their presence should not turn every quiet crossing into a course.

### What has evolved through feedback

V2's world was worth exploring but travel and danger felt weak. V3 made movement and boats more powerful and changed threats to intercept, commit, and leave actionable tells. V4 enlarged and differentiated the world; a subsequent human playtest found the sea too spread out. V5 brought it closer and added inhabitants and sea activities; its feedback praised the map, boats, and creatures but found hoops/coins crowded and oddly placed. V6 rearranged the same offers, measured routes, and repaired global thunder. These are attributed historical findings, not controlled causal experiments or a guarantee of broad player preference.

V6's report was later amended after Ninety discovered the blocked Skull Chalice approach. The source now contains the ladder/hatch repair. Its earlier 'nobody has played V6' wording describes an earlier checkpoint; it must not erase that later feedback. Broader V6 layout, sound-by-ear, multiplayer, mobile, and balance acceptance remain outstanding.

### Current guardrails and absent features

V7 added a small progression layer (Shinies, five pets, start-with-gear kits, a saved profile, an inert Robux receipt foundation). **V11 turned it into Goblin Life**: a 121-item catalogue of goblin cosmetics, boat paint, flags, figureheads, trails, wakes, trick effects, callout styles, emotes and victory dances; five redesigned pets with looks and hats; outfit presets; 11 achievements; a shop and locker with 3D previews; a session-locked, migrating saved profile; and Robux plumbing that stays switched off until a human creates products. Expression over power: nothing sold or earned makes a goblin stronger except the five pets (small sidegrades, all sold for Shinies) and the start kits (gear that is free in the world). **V13** added seven boat classes (two free; five earned with Shinies, each a sidegrade with a weakness: a balance rule is tested), 37 more pets (still only six abilities, every one available on a cheap pet), ten achievements (seven of them grant an island's pet for escaping its creature) and deeds that pay a little for a steal, an escape, a snatch or clean tricks. **V13.3** added Port games, daily and weekly quests, leaderboards with season rewards, sanctuary decoration and pet expeditions, all paying capped Shinies or cosmetics (titles, pennants, sails, pet hats), never power. There is still no XP, trading, crafting, random reward, egg, loot box, login streak or boat upgrade tree. Since 2026-10-14 the scope is open: the team can add any of these whenever they want (see AGENTS.md). The original long-term design vision appears later as inspiration. Rough geometry, primitive creature models, built-in sounds, and incomplete advertised input coverage are prototype compromises; they are not proof of release readiness.

An outside AI should deepen possession and escape, preserve movement agency, compare ideas against existing verbs, and distinguish current V8 from historical configurations. A mechanic rejected for another game is not automatically rejected here. What gets built next is the team's call; a teammate's request is enough.

This approval does not certify outstanding human, multiplayer, audio-by-ear, or device tests. Historical reports below retain their original checkpoint status.

Everything below describes the V13 code: V9's systems (with the V8, V7 and V6 sections they build on) under V10's look, with V11's customization and progression on top, V12's cohesion pass through all of it, V13's Port, fleet, bestiary and quieter screen, V13.1's fixes, V13.2's Sea of Chaos, V13.3's Living Port and V13.4's polish of it, and their current limitations.

## Purpose

Loot Goblins is a Roblox game by Ethan, Ninety and Enrik. The one-sentence thesis is: *steal ridiculous treasure from dangerous islands and other players, then somehow get it home.*

The loop: **explore (awe) → steal treasure → the world reacts → escape (panic) → bank → repeat.** Going out should feel like adventure; coming home with something valuable should feel like needing to GET OUT. V3's aim on top of that: **the player should feel powerful, the world should feel dangerous, and the fun is where those two meet.** Moving and sailing should be enjoyable in themselves, not the price of reaching the fun. V4's aim: **the world should be big and varied enough to deserve that movement**, with geography that is itself something to learn and use. V5's aim: **every island should have something living on it that a player can learn**, and the sea between them should be a playground, not a commute. V6's aim: **placement over quantity.** What the sea offers should be few enough, and laid out plainly enough, that a goblin can see it and choose. V7's aim: **a server of up to 32 should start with a spectacle and have somewhere different to go**: a ship to fall from, sixteen islands that each ask something different, an island robbed makes its neighbours wary, and what a goblin keeps between raids is a sidegrade, not power.

The design principle is **active novelty**: surprises the player participates in (a geyser to time, a ring to jump, a charge to dodge, a storm to steer around), not things that just happen on screen.

The long-term vision later in this document is inspiration, not a plan; the team decides what to build from it.

## Core loop

1. Players gather in the **Goblin Port** (V13) and **sign up** for the next raid (V13.2: only those who join go; 60 s from the first sign-up, or 8 s once everyone signed up is aboard the little airship), start each raid on the **skyship** (V7; since V13.2 it flies a route and its cannons reach about 1,200 studs), dive to an island in reach, and bring treasure to **the Hoard** at **Goblin Cove**. Each raid has one **world-chaos** event (V13.2), named in the Port. A raid is a 42 s launch window (V13.2; was 20 s) and then `Config.RAID_DURATION` (360 s) of clock; then everyone in it comes home to the Port, the winners onto the podium.
2. Nineteen treasures wait on 19 islands (16 major, three keys with small stashes), each with a light pillar; its name and value show within 170 studs (V9; through V8 across the whole map). **Values are flat since V8** (4 to 11 g) with one exception since V9: **the Golden Idol, 17 g**.
3. Prying treasure off its spot (hold E, 0.6 s) adds Heat and triggers that treasure's own **trouble** (a flooding vault, a volcano, the Leviathan, the Ghost Fleet, snapping bridges...). Most big islands also have an **inhabitant** with one rule to learn (see Island inhabitants), and since V9 every one of them **follows the thief to sea almost all the way home** (see V9 systems).
4. The carrier is hunted by the world (see Heat), can be robbed by other players, pays more stamina for every move and slows the boat they sit in. On foot they are only a little slower than anyone else.
5. Carrying treasure into the Hoard ring banks its gold. Banked treasure respawns later; treasure nobody takes grows more valuable (**interest**: `LOOT_INTEREST_SHARE` of its value, at least 1 g, per 45 s since V9, three steps at most).
6. **Coins** on the water are a side dish: ten make 1 gold at the Hoard, at most `COIN_GOLD_CAP` (6) gold a raid. Treasure is the score.
7. When the timer ends, the most gold wins (`Wins` +1). Everything resets.

## Systems

All tuning numbers live in `src/shared/Config.lua`. Gameplay modules never hardcode tuning.

### World and map

- **`Archipelago.lua`** (shared) is the one list of islands (id, name, x, z, radius, ring, colour) and of the sea's **regions** (names for the map). The server builds terrain from it; the client's map, compass and signs read it. North is -Z. The sea is 5880 x 5010 studs (`Config.BOUNDS_*`; V5 and V6 were 5080 x 4390, V4 6900 x 5840); its header explains the regions and why the distances are what they are. V7 moved every island beyond the home ring 20% farther from Goblin Cove along the same line; the islands kept their size. `Config.ISLAND_INFO` lists the sixteen major islands (tier, challenge, gear) and the supporting ones.
- **`World.lua`** builds the environment (sea floor, boundary walls in ≤2000-stud pieces, far-sea horizon slabs, haze) and the eight original islands (Goblin Cove, Crossroads, Sun Temple, Crystal Isle, Shipwreck Shoals, Gull Rock, Smuggler's Cove, Twin Stacks). **Those builders are written in the coordinates they were first built at**; each runs with a build offset (`Kit.setShift`, set by `moved(id, builder)`) that moves it, unchanged, to its place in `Archipelago`. Anything they leave in `refs` goes through `Kit.world` (aliased `W`). Offsets must be multiples of 4 studs (asserted), so the terrain lands on the same voxels. **To move an original island, change its x and z in `Archipelago.lua` in steps of 4; do not edit the builder's coordinates.** Twin Stacks must keep its offset from Crystal Isle (a zipline joins them).
- **`Islands.lua`** (Pebble, Coral Atoll, Windmill Hills, Tide Vault, Smuggler's stash) and **`IslandsFar.lua`** (Fort Barnacle, Tangle Isle, Ember Isle, Maelstrom Rock, Frost Spire, Leviathan's Rest, Skull Rock) already build relative to `Archipelago` and run with no offset.
- **`Landform.lua`** writes natural land into the Terrain voxels from a list of lobes (hills, ridges, mesas, cuts): wobbling coastlines, shelving seabeds, cliff-walled crags. It only adds to what is there. `Landform.shaper(cx, cz, spec)` is the convenient way in. It also makes the horizon **silhouettes** (`Landform.silhouette`, `Landform.mark`). Heights given to it are real heights (it compensates for the two studs the engine adds: see the Studio section).
- **`Outlands.lua`** is the new land around every island (`lands.<Id>`, built BEFORE the island builders so they lay their ground on it and carve their harbors out of it) and what stands on it (`places.<Id>`, built AFTER: docks, spare boats, ziplines, catapults, beacons, the harbor chain, the three new treasures). Offsets there are from the island's center.
- **`Seaways.lua`** is the water between islands: Wrecker's Reef and the Gate, the Western Shelf, the Teeth, the Serpent Channel, the Cinders, lone rocks, currents. **Everything in it is placed from island positions** (`from(id, dx, dz)`, or a point between two islands), never from fixed world coordinates, so it follows when `Archipelago.lua` changes. It exposes what other modules need to find (`Seaways.GATE`, `SHELF`, `TEETH`, `serpent()`, `rock(name)`).
- **`Searuns.lua`** is what is laid on that water: the lanes, the timed courses, the ramps and the coins. **Its header holds the layout rules; read them before adding a hoop** (they are summarized under "Lanes, courses, coins and salvage" below). It fills `refs.boostGates`, `refs.coins`, `refs.runs` (timed courses) and `refs.lanes`, and adds a line to `refs.buildWarnings` (which `Main` prints) for any hoop over water shallower than 3.2 studs.
- **`WorldKit.lua`** holds the shared helpers (parts, terrain shapes, docks, ladders, signs, cannons, bridges, geysers, and V4's `hoop`, `kicker`, `stream`, `hookPost`, `catapult`, `beacon`). It also records where anything was built (`Kit.touch`, exposed as `refs.builtOn`).
- **Builders only describe.** They leave data in `refs` (`breakables`, `barrels`, `kegCrates`, `cannons`, `levers`, `gates`, `beacons`, `spinners`, `geysers`, `lavaZones`, `boostGates`, `coins`, `runs`, `lanes`, `navyBases`, `troubleSites`, `targets`) and the mechanism modules run it. Never put logic in a builder.
- About 8,800 server parts since V10 (V9: about 6,000; the skyship is about 400 with its V10 dressing, the 16 landmarks about 630) and 43 boats, 101 gates (95 hoops, 6 ramps), 132 coins. **The world takes 3 to 4 s to build and the sea grid another 3 s** (V3: 3 s in all); `Main` prints both with a breakdown at start-up. Watch that line when you add terrain.
- **Depths that matter:** a skiff needs 3.1 studs of water, a cutter 3.9, a patrol ship 5.6 (`SeaNav`: draft + 1.8). Reef crest 1.2, reef passes 3.7, the Western Shelf 4.8. **Green lamps mark water a patrol ship cannot enter; gold lamps mark the Gate.** Keep that language if you add shallows.
- **Folders** under `workspace.LootGoblinsGenerated`: `Ground` (walkable; the Guardian walks on it), `Structures` (boats live here), `Decor`, `Loot`, `Threats`, `Effects` (also mines and waterspouts), `Coins` (coins and salvage crates), `SpiritBodies`, `LaunchPads` (also geyser vents), `Ziplines`, `Landmarks` (persistent: island signs, `HoardMarker`, the horizon silhouettes, the skyship and, since V10, each island's `Landmark<Id>` model and Frost Spire's `Aurora`).
- **Streaming is on** (`default.project.json`: min 256, target 2048). Loot models, island signs, the Hoard marker and the silhouettes are `Persistent`; everything else streams. Client code must never assume far parts exist. The far islands are thousands of studs from home, so the silhouettes (plain blocks buried inside each island's tall ground, built in the background after start-up by `World.buildHorizon`) are what a far island looks like. With the islands closer, more of the world sits inside the streaming radius (a client at the Crossroads holds about 6,800 world instances).
- **Signs** made with `Kit.sign` are tagged `RangedSign`, and the client hides one that is really farther than its `MaxDistance` (Roblox measures a billboard's distance along the line of sight, so signs far off to one side would all show). Give a new sign the range you mean.

### Sea (`shared/Sea.lua`, `SeaNav.lua`, `Storms.lua`)

- `Sea` is pure math: `waveAt(x, z, t)` (three crossing swells), `currentAt` (wind drift + streams + whirlpools), `stormAt`, `shelterAt`. Swell is calmer beside land (shelter) and wild in a storm. The Terrain water is only the visual surface.
- **`Sea` is shared** (`ReplicatedStorage.LootGoblins.Sea`) because a driven boat floats on the driver's client. `src/server/Sea.lua` only forwards to it. The server sends the static half once (`ReplicatedStorage.LootGoblinsSea`, a JSON StringValue: streams, whirlpools, the shelter grid as one digit per cell, the boat gates), and `Sea.follow()` on the client keeps the storms and the global roughness current from `workspace.StormData` and `workspace.SeaRough`.
- **Currents** (`Kit.stream`, readable chevrons): Rushing Strait, Temple Drift, Cinder Run, Northern Drift, Mill Race, the Serpent Channel (the fastest, 28), and the Maelstrom whirlpool (strongest at mid-radius, calm in the eye).
- `SeaNav` builds a 40-stud grid from the finished terrain: water depth per cell, distance to land (shelter), and A* routes. **It only raycasts where a builder touched the map** (`refs.builtOn`, plus one cell of margin); everywhere else is taken to be open water 26 deep. A raycast on untouched terrain makes the engine build its collision, and doing that for the whole sea cost five seconds of start-up. Anything that raises the seabed must therefore go through `Kit.terrain`, `Kit.part` into `Ground`, or `Landform` (they record it); a raw `workspace.Terrain` call would be invisible to ships. A hull can only use cells deeper than its draft + 1.8, so deep ships cannot cross shallows. `SeaNav.path` takes a coast weight; the Navy uses a strong one so its fast, wide-turning ships keep off headlands.
- **Storms**: moving cells (rough water, wind, lightning). After a 50 s calm, up to `STORM_MAX_AMBIENT` (3) ambient ones at once, a new one every 45–75 s, **seeded 600–1050 studs from a player who is out at sea and set to blow across them** (never within `STORM_HOME_CLEAR` of the Hoard), at 16–28 studs/s; Maelstrom's treasure calls a squall; FRENZY heat sends a hunting **tempest** at 42 (slower than any boat, faster than anyone on foot); Skull Rock calls **fog**. Published as one string attribute `workspace.StormData`. Lightning is **marked** 1.3 s ahead. `Storms.Spent` fires where an ambient storm blows itself out (salvage listens).
- **Waterspouts**: each storm cell carries two (the tempest three) circling its heart. Server parts in `Effects`. One flings any boat or goblin it catches upward and sideways (`SPOUT_*`).

### Boats (`shared/BoatSim.lua`, `server/Boats.lua`, `client/BoatDrive.lua`)

- **`BoatSim.step(boat, input, dt, t)` is the physics**, shared, and runs on whichever machine owns the hull. Forces: buoyancy springs at six hull points toward `Sea.waveAt`; thrust (only while wet) with a launch punch and a real brake; an arcade keel that redirects drift instead of braking; a yaw-rate target; banking; an upright assist; drag toward the water's own flow. It **measures** how much Roblox's Terrain water slows the hull and cancels it under power, so `maxSpeed` in Config is the speed actually reached, on any hull at any frame rate.
- **Drift**: `input.drift` held in a turn at speed lowers the grip, swings the hull out to a slide angle and holds it there, and charges `driftCharge`; releasing pays a burst (`BOAT_MINI_KICK`, two levels). **Landing**: after `BOAT_AIR_MIN` seconds off the water, an upright, straight touchdown gives a burst. **Capsize**: a hull upside down for `BOAT_FLIP_TIME` pops upright.
- **Who simulates** (`Config.BOAT_CLIENT_PHYSICS`, default true): an empty or AI boat, the server; a boat with a driver, **the driver's client** (`BoatDrive` runs `BoatSim` in `PreSimulation`, reading the seat's `ThrottleFloat`/`SteerFloat`). The server calls `hull:SetNetworkOwner(driver)` and sets the model's `Pilot` attribute. With the setting off the server simulates everything, as V2 did.
- **`Boats.lua` (server) stays in charge:** hull health, crashes, scrapes, repair, sinking, respawn, anchors, seats, boost cooldowns, sleeping far boats. `watchHull` measures crashes on every hull from its velocity (a change over `BOAT_IMPACT_WINDOW` that the engine and keel cannot explain). `police` checks every driven hull each frame (speed, altitude, jumps) and takes it back for `BOAT_RECLAIM_TIME` if it breaks a rule.
- **Rules for code that touches boats:** to push a hull use `Boats.shove` (a driven hull is pushed by telling its driver's client); to move one use `Boats.place` (it takes the hull back first); to hurt one use `Boats.damage` or a `Blast`. Never write a driven hull's velocity or CFrame directly from the server.
- Types in `Config.BOAT_TYPES`: **skiff** (135, the best drifter, fragile), **cutter** (104, cannon, 3 passengers, shrugs off crashes, rams hard), **navy** patrol ship (106, wide turns, deep draft, AI only, no bow skid, **white** with a blue stripe). V6's numbers were 108, 86 and 88; turn rate and its fade with speed were raised so chain-speed turning is no worse.
- **Hop, land, recall (V7).** `input.jump` hops a hull that has water or ground under it (`BOAT_JUMP_*`). A hull on the ground (`boat.grounded`, a raycast under it) drives at `BOAT_LAND_SPEED` of its top speed (about 22 studs/s measured; a boost does not raise it), and reversing backs it off a steep beach. `Recall.lua` (B) brings the nearest free boat, or builds a skiff (at most `RECALL_EXTRA_MAX`), to the nearest shore: placed `RECALL_OFFSHORE` studs out and driven in by the same physics.
- **Beaching**: player hulls carry an invisible sloped `BowSkid` so they ride up gentle shores. V7 boats drive on land slowly (see above); a steep step (about 30 degrees) still stops a hull, and reversing takes it back to the sea.
- **Gates**: boost hoops and kicker ramps from `refs.boostGates`, applied by the simulating machine (`BoatSim.gate`); the server broadcasts the effect. A hoop made with `Kit.hoop` pushes whichever way the boat is already going (`both`) unless it is made one-way. A kicker must stand in open water: one built on a sandbar stalls the boat.
- **Hoop chains** (in `BoatSim.gate`, so they run on whichever machine owns the hull): a hoop within `BOAT_CHAIN_WINDOW` (4 s) of the last one kicks `BOAT_CHAIN_KICK` harder per link, up to `BOAT_CHAIN_MAX` links. **A kick never takes a boat past a ceiling** (boosted top speed plus `BOAT_CHAIN_TOP` per link: 151 to 175 for a skiff). Without it a chain down a current reached 257 studs/s, above what `police` allows. Keep the ceiling if you add kicks. **At chain speed a skiff barely steers** (about 180 studs of turning radius, and its course lags its bow): that is what the layout rules below are built on.
- `Boats.refund(boat, seconds)` shortens a boost cooldown (attribute `BoostRefund` tells the driver's client); `Boats.patch(boat, amount)` repairs a hull.
- AI boats take `boat.input = {throttle, steer, boost}` (see Navy).

### Treasure, Heat and consequences

- **Loot** (`Loot.lua`): 19 treasures in `Config.LOOT` (id, island, value, weight, carry speed, heat, respawn, trouble, visual). States `spot`, `carried` (welded above the head), `loose` (server physics; floats), `away` (banked). Steal immunity after any change of hands. **Interest**: untouched treasure gains value (`bonus`); banking pays `item.bankedValue`. **Treasure a creature carries stays `loose`**: `Loot.hold(item, cframe)` pins it (`item.held`), `Loot.letGo(item, velocity)` drops it, `Loot.sendHome(item, reason)` puts it back on its spot. So anyone can still grab it and every existing rule keeps working; do not add a state for it.
- **Heat** (`Heat.lua`): shared 0–100, tiers CALM, ALERT (25), HUNTED (50), FRENZY (80). It rises on theft and while carrying outside the ward (`HEAT_CARRY_RATE` 0.62: V4 was 0.48 on a sea with trips 30% longer); falls while nobody carries.
- **Escalation** (`Escalation.lua`) is what each tier *does*:
  - **ALERT**: carriers fire flares every 6 s that every player sees; totems and Fort turrets wake; carriers glow through walls.
  - **HUNTED**: a Navy **hunter** comes for the most valuable carrier; the Guardian hunts.
  - **FRENZY**: a second ship (a **blocker**) takes the way home and lays mines; a tempest steers at the thief; rougher sea everywhere.
  - Dropping below HUNTED stands the Navy down.
- **Threats** (`Threats.lua`): the Guardian (kinematic golem; walks Terrain and `Ground`, wades; speed 27, 32 at FRENZY; leashed to 520 studs from the temple's center until FRENZY, which is the whole of the bigger island). Its moves, all announced: **stomp** (fists up 0.8 s, then a ring races outward along the ground and hits only players standing on something as it passes: jump it), **leap** to a marked circle, **boulder throw** at a marked circle. Also totems, rollers, carrier reveal. Handlers for new trouble plug into `Threats.handlers`.
- **Troubles** (`Troubles.lua`) — one per treasure:

  | Treasure | Trouble |
  | --- | --- |
  | Lost Compass, Giant Pearl, Sunken Sextant, Castaway's Hoard | Gulls: the thief is revealed to everyone for 10 s |
  | Smuggler's Stash, Lighthouse Lens, Storm Lantern | Bell: the thief is revealed for 20 s |
  | Golden Gear | The windmill spins up (blades sweep the balcony) |
  | Captain's Chest | The wreck's cannon barrage |
  | Crystal Heart | Cave-in seals the tunnel |
  | Jade Frog | Quake: the rope bridges snap |
  | Pearl of the Deep | The vault floods to just below the top of its stairway (V8: the way out is the way in, up the stairs; or a grapple through the skylight) and the Warden follows a thief to sea |
  | Tempest Trident | A squall settles on the whirlpool |
  | Admiral's Strongbox | Two patrol ships launch at once (if the fort's harbor chain is up, the moment it drops) |
  | Ember Crown | The volcano rains marked lava bombs |
  | Golden Idol | The Guardian wakes and a boulder rolls |
  | Aurora Gem | Snow boulders roll down the glacier |
  | Leviathan Tooth | V8: the Leviathan hunts the thief once they put to sea (V7: tentacle strikes round the island) |
  | Skull Chalice | Fog, and a ghost fleet (18 s late if the Captain's shade is dozing: see Island inhabitants) |

- **Navy** (`Navy.lua`): AI patrol ships on `SeaNav` routes after the most valuable carrier they can *see* (line of sight, range 700, shorter in storms).
  - **Where they come from:** the fort if it is within `NAVY_BASE_RANGE` (1150: Navy Waters) of the thief, otherwise open deep water on the horizon, 750–950 studs out, on the thief's side of home and in sight.
  - **The harbor chain:** while the fort's chain is raised (`base.chain.progress`), `Navy.dispatch` sends nothing from the fort. Ships already out are not affected.
  - **Beacons:** `Navy.distract(position)` makes every patrol ship within `BEACON_RANGE` ignore carriers for `BEACON_TIME` and sail to that position.
  - **Roles:** a **hunter** sails an intercept (where the thief will be), runs alongside at `NAVY_STATION` firing, and charges. A **blocker** sits `NAVY_BLOCK_AHEAD` studs along the thief's line home and sows **mines** (`Navy.layMine`), then turns hunter when the thief is close. Every second ship is a blocker.
  - **Shells** land where a marker closes in over 1.5 s; up close it is a spread of three along the thief's course.
  - **The charge:** a horn (`NavyRam` event), then `NAVY_RAM_TIME` seconds on one bearing aimed where the thief will be if they hold course. It is not corrected, so turning dodges it. Then the ship swings wide before closing again.
  - **Mines:** bright, still, 40 s lifetime, go off for any hull or swimmer, and any blast sets off the mines it reaches (`Blast.Hit`).
  - They lose you behind islands or in the shallows (the reef passes and the whole Western Shelf are closed to them), search your last position for 25 s, then leave. They can be sunk. Carriers inside the Hoard ward are unreachable.
- **Blast** (`Blast.lua`): every explosion goes through `Blast.at` (players, boats, loose loot, destructibles) and fires `Blast.Hit`. `Blast.strike` shows a marker first. The blast's owner takes the shove at half strength and no damage (a keg at your feet is a launcher). A player sitting in a boat is moved with the hull, not separately.

### Lanes, courses, coins and salvage (`Searuns.lua`, `Coins.lua`)

- **The layout rules** (V6; the V5 playtest found the same content fun and badly placed):
  - **A teal hoop is a lane.** It points at a dock across open water, straight unless there is a reason to bend, a hoop about every 190 studs, with a small sign at each end saying where it leads. 13 of them (`refs.lanes`).
  - **An orange hoop is a timed course**, set apart from the lanes: a run threaded through stacks (The Teeth, Cinder Slalom), a sprint down a current (Serpent Run), or a lap round a landmark (Lookout Loop, Maelstrom Ring).
  - **A coin marks a line worth taking**: a weave through a course, a stack to hug, the air over a ramp, a trail into somewhere hidden. Six long lanes carry one between hoops. Coins never just fill water.
  - **Home Bay is calm**: one line of hoops from the harbor through the Gate. Some water (the fort's, the skull's, the far east, the south) has no lane at all, on purpose.
  - **A line of hoops must hardly bend.** A chain holds a skiff at 150 to 175 studs a second. Driven, a boat stayed on a line that bent 8 degrees at a gate and left one that bent 24. Keep to about 10 degrees a gate at 150 studs apart; a lap needs about 300 studs of radius; and **where the way really twists, use coins, not hoops** (the channel across the Western Shelf is a coin trail for this reason).
  - **A lane must not deliver a boat onto an island's threat.** The Leviathan Road stops 300 studs short of the Sleeper.
- **Coins** are server parts in the `Coins` folder with a `Value` attribute (1, or 5 for the big ones). `Coins.tick` checks every driven hull and every goblin on foot against a 64-stud grid of coins 20 times a second, and also half way back to the last check, so nothing is skipped at speed. Reach: `COIN_BOAT_REACH` 13, `COIN_FOOT_REACH` 7. **The client never claims a coin**; it only hides one a moment early so the pickup feels instant.
- **A coin right now:** `COIN_BOOST_REFUND` off the boat's boost cooldown and `COIN_REPAIR` hull. **A coin later:** the purse (`Coins` attribute) pays 1 gold per `COINS_PER_GOLD` at the Hoard, at most `COIN_GOLD_CAP` a raid (`CoinGold` attribute). A taken coin comes back after `COIN_RESPAWN`. Everything resets with the raid. There is nothing to spend coins on, and there must not be. All 132 coins are worth 240, four times one goblin's cap.
- **Timed courses** (`refs.runs`): a course starts at the hoop at either end and wants every hoop in order. A **lap** (`loop = true`) starts and ends at its first hoop, either way round; the clock keeps running for the next lap, and crossing the line with hoops missed starts a new one. A course pays `RUN_COINS` once a raid and `RUN_PAR_COINS` more the first time under par, and keeps the best time and name on its sign for the session. **Pars are measured** (the `PAR` table in `Searuns.lua`): a clean run by the test autopilot plus 15 to 20 percent. Change a course and measure its par again.
- **Salvage** (`Coins.dropSalvage(position, why)`): a floating crate worth `SALVAGE_COINS`, a keg, `SALVAGE_REPAIR` hull and a boost refill. `Main` drops one where a patrol ship sinks (`Boats.Sunk`) and where a storm blows out (`Storms.Spent`); `SALVAGE_ADRIFT` are set adrift each raid 45 to 70 studs to one side of a lane (never the Gate Run: Home Bay stays calm).

### Island inhabitants (`Creatures.lua`, `Bestiary.lua`, `BestiaryMinor.lua`)

- **`Creatures.lua` is the shared machinery; a creature is a table** registered with `Creatures.add({ name, island, home, wake, build, tick, reset, onTaken, onBlast })`. Numbers live in `Config.CREATURES`. To add one, copy the smallest (the clam or the fin in `BestiaryMinor.lua`).
- What the framework gives: `Creatures.body` (one anchored root, everything else welded, so moving it is one CFrame write), `pose`, `walk` (follows the ground; an `allowed` callback can refuse a step), `floor`, `canSee`, `players`, `carriers`, `nearest`, `looseLoot`, `strike` (**the one way a creature touches a player**: damage, push, knock loot loose, toast), `mark` (the ring), `fx` (a `Creature` GameEvent the client turns into a sound and a puff).
- **Sleep:** a creature is ticked only while a player is within its `wake` radius of its `home`, or while it sets `busy` (carrying treasure back, say). A test that does not put a player in range will see nothing happen.
- **Kinematic, like the Guardian:** no collisions, no raycast hits. They walk through walls and props.
- **Hooks:** `Creatures.onTaken(item, player, fromSpot)` is called from `Loot.Taken` in `Main`; `onBlast` from `Blast.Hit` (a keg stops every creature that can be stopped); `Creatures.reset()` from `Raid.resetWorld`. `Creatures.generation` is bumped on reset so a delayed action from an old raid never lands.
- **The rule for a new creature:** one idea a player can learn, a visible tell, no stun, no instant kill, nothing that leaves its island, and not the Guardian with a different skin.

  | Island | Creature | Rule | Effect |
  | --- | --- | --- | --- |
  | Crossroads Ruins | The Watchers (4) | Move only while no goblin within 170 studs is facing them | Touch knocks loot loose; one carries it back to its spot (slowly, and it can be taken from its arms) |
  | Crystal Isle | The Echo | Retraces the carrier's path 3 s behind | 16 damage, loot loose, to anyone it walks into |
  | Shipwreck Shoals | Old Clacker (crab) | Travels only under sand and shallows; a ring 0.85 s before it comes up | Toss, 10 damage, loot loose; reburies loose treasure it reaches |
  | Windmill Hills | Bramble (ram) | Charges in a straight line after a 0.9 s windup; only at goblins ashore | Long toss, 6 damage. Dazed if it hits a cliff. Rages after the Gear is taken |
  | Tide Vault | The Warden (eel) | Circles the shallows; hunts whoever is in the water for 30 s after the pearl is taken | 12 damage, loot loose, in water only |
  | Tangle Isle | **The Jade Frogs** (3, V13.1; were the imps) | Bound after a carrier anywhere on the island; a ring where you are (0.75 s), then a pounce | A belly slam: 12 damage, a toss, and a carrier hit (Config.KNOCKOUT). They hop into the sea after you |
  | Fort Barnacle | The Garrison (2 marines) | A drawn vision cone on a patrol route | Whistle, charge, throws the goblin over the wall. No damage |
  | Ember Isle | Cinderlings (3) | Run to where a carrier is heading | Lay fire patches (8 damage per half second). Never touch the player |
  | Frost Spire | The Chill | A drifting cold that follows climbers; V13.1: chases a carrier anywhere on the island at 44 | `Movement.chill`: stamina drains. V13.1 **hail**: a ring where the carrier is going (1 s), then ice: 12 damage, a carrier hit, stamina chilled. It follows them into the sea |
  | Leviathan's Rest | The Sleeper | Wakes to boats faster than 45 studs/s | Three marked tentacle strikes at the loudest boat (45 hull) |
  | Skull Rock | The Captain's shade | Eyes lit 16 s, dark 9 s, by the clock | Chalice taken while dark: the ghost fleet is 18 s late (it wraps `Threats.handlers.GhostFleet`) |
  | Maelstrom Rock | The Maw (fin) | Circles the whirlpool | Shoves boats (`Boats.shove`). No damage |
  | Coral Atoll | The Clam | Open 5 s, shut 3 s | The Giant Pearl's prompt only works while open; shut on a goblin: toss, 8 damage |
  | Goblin Cove | Gobbo | Friendly | A keg every 25 s; warns in the feed of a patrol ship or storm near home |

  The Sun Temple keeps the Guardian (`Threats.lua`). Pebble Isle, Gull Rock, Smuggler's Cove, Twin Stacks and the three keys have nothing living on them.

### Interactive island pieces

- **Destructibles** (`Destructibles.lua`): cracked walls (any blast), gates (cannonball), rope bridges (any blast, or a quake), powder barrels (chain reactions). Broken pieces become debris and are rebuilt from stored copies on reset.
- **Cannons** (`Cannons.lua`): island emplacements (Fort Barnacle's wall, the home practice range) and the Cutter. `E` fires where you aim; the server validates range, cooldown and aim, solves the arc and flies the ball.
- **Kegs** (`Kegs.lua`): `KEG_MAX` per player from crates, thrown with `G`, fuse 2 s.
- **Mechanisms** (`Mechanisms.lua`): the windmill's sweeping blades, the Maelstrom's foam spirals, levers and gates, lava that burns, and **signal beacons** (`Mechanisms.light`; fires `Mechanisms.BeaconLit`, which `Main` wires to `Navy.distract`). A gate entry may carry `hold` (seconds it stays moved) and `pulled` (the feed text): **Fort Barnacle's harbor chain** is a gate whose "open" position is raised across the harbor mouth.
- **Catapults** (`Kit.catapult`) are launch pads with a `Carry` attribute: the client holds the throw's sideways speed for that many seconds (a goblin's own air control would stop it short). Dash, air jump, a grapple or a zipline ends it. **Geysers** are animated and launch on the **client** from timestamps (attributes on the vent), so the server does nothing per frame.

### Movement, combat, spirit, raid

- **Movement** (`Movement.lua`): the only writer of `WalkSpeed`; owns stamina. Running (28) is free; since V13.2 this is the BASE speed (published as `MoveCap`), which the goblin's own client multiplies by its momentum (`shared/Momentum.lua`, up to ×1.36). There is no sprint. Stamina pays for dash, air jump and a carrier's sword swing; `Movement.spend` scales every cost by the held treasure's weight (`CARRY_STAMINA_PER_WEIGHT`). `Movement.request(player, "dash" | "airjump")` is the client asking the server to pay for a move it already played. `Movement.chill(player, seconds)` stops regeneration and drains stamina (`CHILL_REGEN`, `CHILL_DRAIN`; attribute `Chilled`).
- **Combat**: sword (carriers swing slowly and tiredly), grapple. **V7: a grapple at a carrier catches, it does not rob**: `Combat.catch` knocks them down (`PlatformStand`, yanked toward the thrower, `DownedUntil` attribute, 2 s, then 6 s of immunity), and `Combat.stealFrom` (the E key, sent by a prompt the client builds on a goblin who is down) validates the thief, distance, line of sight, the hold and the throw cooldown before `Loot.steal`. The Hoard's ward protects. A pet Shell Tortoise absorbs one catch per 30 s. The grapple pull follows a moving anchor; aim that passes near a moving boat catches the boat (`GRAPPLE_BOAT_ASSIST`), and the server seats the player on the boat it hooked for them (`Combat.hookedBoat`).
- **Poltergoblin**: switched off since V13.1 (`Config.POLTER_ENABLED`); the module is kept for a later return.
- **Raid** (`Raid.lua`): phases, scoring, `resetWorld()` resets every system (loot, Heat, threats, Navy and its mines, storms and their spouts, destructibles, mechanisms, cannons, kegs, boats, flood, coins and salvage, creatures).
- `Players.CharacterAutoLoads` is off until the world is built, then everyone is loaded.

### Client

- `Hud.lua`: timer, Heat bar, sorted treasure board (with interest), feed, banner, objective line, ability slots (sword, throw, grapple, keg, Poltergoblin; stamina and dash bottom-left), boat panel (speed, hull, boost, **drift meter**, hoop chain, anchor, cargo drag), the coin purse above the stamina bar, the controls card. V12: banners go through `BannerQueue.lua`, the objective line through `Objective.lua`, and `Hud.mode()` (ship, flight, boat, foot) decides which parts show.
- V12: `Danger.lua` (red arrows for whatever chases you), `TouchControls.lua` (touch buttons), `BannerQueue.lua` and `Objective.lua` (pure, tested).
- `BoatDrive.lua`: runs `BoatSim` on the boat you drive; boost and drift input; applies server pushes and boost refunds; reports hoop chains to the HUD; draws every nearby boat's wake and spray.
- `Map.lua`: the world map (`M`) and the **compass strip** (Hoard, treasures, storms).
- `Weather.lua`: reads `StormData`; draws cloud walls, fog, rain and darkening; sets wave size; warns "STORM TO THE NORTH-EAST - 600 STUDS".
- `Effects.lua`: sounds from `rbxasset://sounds/*`, neon effects, **markers** (a closing ring on the ground: the one visual language for "this lands here"), the Guardian's shockwave, lightning bolts, flares, shells, tentacles, fireworks, dash and air-jump puffs. The field of view follows speed (`Effects.setSpeed`) and kicks for a dash or a launch (`punchFov`); one writer per frame. **Sound has two kinds**, and `Effects.sound` decides by whether it is given a position: an INTERFACE sound (a chime, an alarm) plays in the player's ears; a WORLD sound plays at its place with `InverseTapered` rolloff, fades to silence at its `range`, and is **not played at all** beyond it or when it would be inaudible. At most `VOICE_LIMIT` of one sound start within `VOICE_WINDOW`, and the world's sound group has a compressor. Thunder is a world sound (`Effects.thunder`). Far-off markers, blasts and bolts are not drawn either. Numbers: `Config.AUDIO`.
- `Main.client.lua`: input, momentum (V13.2), dash, air jump, the grapple swing and pull (V13.2), the bow gun click, zipline/pad/geyser movement, cannon and keg input, hiding coins the moment you pass them, hiding signs that are out of range, creature sounds and puffs (`CREATURE_FX`), event routing.

## V13.4: The Living Port, polished

V13.4 answers Ninety's follow-up brief: **make what V13.3 built feel finished and worth returning to, and make the raid leaderboards the Port's centrepiece**, with no new major system and no new game. Built on branch `feature/v13-4-port-polish`, stacked on `feature/v13-3-living-port` (V13.3's PR #28 was still unmerged). Report, evidence and the human playtest checklist: `docs/reports/2026-10-23-v13-4-port-polish.md`. **Nobody has played V13.4**: as the brief asked it was checked by code review, StyLua, Selene, both Rojo builds and the Luau tests in Studio's Edit mode (see the report), not by AI playthroughs.

### The raid boards and the Hall of Legends (`shared/Seasons.lua`, `server/Leaderboards.lua`, client `PortBoard.lua`, `PortHud.lua`, `NextUp.lua`)

- **Three raid boards, listed first everywhere** (`board.raid`): the weekly **BIGGEST HAUL** (one raid, unchanged), the new weekly **PIRATE CHAMPIONSHIP** (board id `crown`: a goblin's best `Config.SEASONS.WEEK_RAIDS` = 3 raids of the week added up, so more raids never win by themselves) and the monthly **PIRATE LEGENDS** (V13.3's monthly Pirate Championship renamed: the **same id `champion`**, the same best five raids, so its DataStore, the Hall's final records, the goblins' saved bests and any unpaid rewards carry over untouched). The Port's game boards (Regatta, Golf, Gauntlet) stay, smaller, as PORT RECORDS. Every board has an icon (💰 👑 🏆 ⛵ ⛳ 🪝).
- **The week's raids are saved like the month's**: `profile.season.week = { key, list }` beside `season.raids` (`Seasons.addRaid` returns the month's and the week's new sums; both bounded lists). A V13.3 profile without it is repaired to an empty week (`ProfileSchema`, `PersistenceSpec`); `Economy.mergePort` merges both lists from a busy profile.
- **Prizes** (catalogue `award` sources, all `rarity = "season"`, never sold): PIRATE CHAMPIONSHIP #1 the **Captain of the Week** title, top 10 the Leaderboard Pennant and the new **Champion's Standard** flag (crimson, three gold stars), gold tier (80) the **Lucky Doubloon** pet hat; PIRATE LEGENDS keeps the Pirate Champion title (#1), Championship Contender and Champion's Sails (top 10) and adds **Legend's Gilt** sails for its gold tier (130). Tiers (Shinies by the goblin's own score, anyone can reach them) and placements are V13.3's rules: weekly 25 / 50 / 80 gold for the Championship's bronze / silver / gold. Rewards are still paid once into the profile after the period ends.
- **A place shows at once**: a goblin's place is their saved best set among the board's last read (`Seasons.rankAmong`: others strictly better, their own old row not counted, nil past 100), not two minutes later at the next read. `BoardBest` carries the new place and the old; the Port records' toast says "⛵ FASTEST REGATTA: 41.20 s · #12 ▲".
- **The Hall of Legends** (V13.3's Hall of Records, rebuilt where it stood, behind the podium facing the plaza): a stone stage, the three raid boards in the middle on gilded pillars (each: the time left, the top eight with the podium in gold, silver and bronze and friends ★, the best goblin in this Port, YOU with your place, and what #1 wins), **PAST CHAMPIONS** on the left (last week's and month's top three on every raid board), the three PORT RECORDS boards on the right, the great HALL OF LEGENDS sign with a lit golden trophy on top, and two braziers. **Climbing into a raid board's top three** puts a line in everyone's feed ("👑 Ninety is #2 on the PIRATE CHAMPIONSHIP!") and sets off fireworks over the Hall.
- **On screen**: the Quest Board panel's second page is **🏆 LEGENDS**: a card per raid board (its icon and name, the time left, your place big, your score and tier, a bar to the next tier, the prizes in one line), then the Port records one line each. The Port screen has a **🏆 chip** showing your best raid place ("🏆 Legends #4 💰") that opens it.
- **After a raid** (`Prospects`, `NextUp`): the card lists the raid boards this raid touched as places with how far they moved ("💰 #4 BIGGEST HAUL ▲5", "👑 #9 PIRATE CHAMPIONSHIP NEW!"), from `Leaderboards.lastMoves`; **⚔ RAID AGAIN** is now the first button, gold and gently pulsing.

### The games, polished (`server/Minigames.lua`, the game modules, client `PlayHud.lua`, `PlayCritters.lua`)

- **No waiting to retry**: a lobby has **▶ START NOW** (`PlayRequest "ready"`); once everyone in it has pressed it the countdown starts at once. On the results card **AGAIN / REMATCH is also `R`** (gamepad `Y`).
- **A target every run**: the play panel's title shows your personal best before this heat (`Minigames.bestOf`, published as the roster's `b`). The countdown ticks; GO flashes. In a points game, passing your best flashes **★ NEW BEST!**.
- **Splits**: in the Regatta and the Gauntlet every checkpoint chimes and, after your first finished run this visit, flashes the split against your best run of the visit (green −0.84, red +1.10; kept on the client only).
- **The results card says how close it came**: a best by how much ("★ NEW BEST! −1.34 s"), otherwise how far off ("+2.10 s off your best (41.23 s)", "6 short of your best"), and the next medal to chase ("🥈 SILVER at 43.00 s").
- **Tiny Boat Regatta**: a **ROCKET START**: throttle down within a quarter second of GO (and not held through the countdown) is a 1.1 s boost (`Config.PLAYGROUND.REGATTA.LAUNCH`; too early flashes WHEELSPIN and gives nothing). The client sends `launch` on GO and the server takes it once, only within `LAUNCH_LATE` (0.6 s) of GO. Overtaking flashes your new place ("▲ 2ND").
- **Grapple Gauntlet**: **shortcuts count**: landing on any platform further on credits every platform before it (`PortGames.gauntletReached`) and flashes ⚡ SHORTCUT!; the respawn is the furthest platform reached. `MIN_TIME` still refuses impossible runs.
- **Pet Derby**: a **timing bar** under the cue (red too soon, green clean, gold **PERFECT**); a perfect cheer (`DERBY.PERFECT_EARLY` 0.28 s before to `PERFECT_LATE` 0.08 s after the hurdle) is a longer burst (`PERFECT_TIME` 1.8 s) and the pet **somersaults** the hurdle; three clean jumps in a row put a pet **ON FIRE** (🔥 on its name, flames, `FIRE` 1.7× instead of 1.5× during bursts) until a tumble or a mashed cheer; and **a commentator** calls the race for everyone at the oval (a new leader, the leader tumbling, a pet on fire, the final stretch, a photo finish, the winner), at most one line every 2.2 s, picked by the race (`PetDerby.call`). Bots are never perfect; every pet still runs the same speed and nothing is bought.
- **Treasure Toss and the Target Gallery**: **streaks**: from the third hit in a row each hit scores one more (`Config.PLAYGROUND.STREAK`, `PortGames.rangeShot`), with a 🔥 x4 STREAK flash; a miss (when it lands) ends it.
- **Crab Chaos**: the play panel shows how many crabs are still loose (the team bonus goal) and flashes 3 / 2 / LAST CRAB!
- Cannon Golf is unchanged apart from the shared panel and results improvements.

### The Port, quests, challenges and the sanctuary

- **Finding the way** (`Port.buildWayfinding`): a signpost on the plaza with a coloured arm pointing at every game, the Hall of Legends, the Quest Board, the pet isles' lift and the raids' airship, and a tall flag in each game's own colour with its icon over every venue, so a goblin can follow a colour across town. Decoration only (nothing solid).
- **Quests**: CLAIM ALL when two or more are ready; a claim pops "+18 ◆" in the middle of the screen with a chime (`QuestClaimed` now carries the Shinies); the panel's small print is down to one line about the week's prize.
- **Challenges**: the result banner shows both scores ("⚔ YOU BEAT NINETY! · 38.21 s vs 40.10 s"; a tie is a DEAD HEAT); when the other goblin asks for a rematch first, an ACCEPT card appears for the rematch's 15 s (the results card may be gone by then).
- **Sanctuary**: stepping onto your own isle, your pets come running to greet you and hop round you for a few seconds. Passive income is unchanged.

### Economy (V13.4)

Nothing V13.3 pays changed except: the new weekly board's tiers and placements (the existing weekly amounts: 10 / 20 / 35 tier Shinies and 15 to 100 for a place), its cosmetics, and the range streak bonus (a point a hit from the third in a row, inside the existing daily caps of 6 paid runs and 40 Shinies a game day). A goblin who plays raids and places on boards could earn about 35 more Shinies a week from the Championship's tier; raids stay well over half of all earnings. Exploit checks: the week's raid list is bounded (best 3) and saved in the profile; the rocket start is accepted once per race and only just after GO; a shortcut still has to reach the platforms and pass `MIN_TIME`; streak points pay through the same capped run rewards.

## V13.3: The Living Port

V13.3 answers Ninety's brief after a playtester enjoyed the raids but was not moved to play past a round or two: **give a goblin reasons to play another five minutes, another raid and another day, through active novelty, progression, social competition and collecting, never through chores.** It turns the Port into a playground: seven games on one framework, the Captain's Quest Board, weekly and monthly leaderboards in a Hall of Records, a floating pet sanctuary for every goblin with pet expeditions, challenges between goblins, and a "what's next" card after every raid. No new currency: everything pays Shinies, small and capped. Every raid, boat, pet, chaos event and V13.2 rule is unchanged. Report, evidence and the human playtest checklist: `docs/reports/2026-10-22-v13-3-living-port.md`. **Nobody has played V13.3**: it was checked by lint, builds, 136 automated Luau tests and one start of Play with an empty console (section "How V13.3 was validated" below).

### The games framework (`server/Minigames.lua`, `shared/PortGames.lua`, client `PlayHud.lua`, `Config.PLAYGROUND`)

- **One framework, seven small modules.** A game registers `{ id, build, prepare, go, tick, input, drop, stop, public, spot }` and the framework does joining, lobbies, the countdown, standings, leaving, results, rewards and publishing. Each game is only what makes it itself (`Regatta`, `Gauntlet`, `CannonGolf`, `PetDerby`, `TreasureToss`, `TargetGallery`, `CrabChaos`).
- **Joining**: `E` at the venue's sign (a ProximityPrompt carrying `PlayGame`), AGAIN on the results, or a challenge. Only a goblin in the Port, alive, not watching the raid and in no other game. **Heat games** (Regatta, Derby, Toss, Gallery, Crab Chaos) run one heat at a time: the first goblin opens a lobby of `LOBBY` (8 s) for others to step in; anyone arriving during a heat is queued for the next. **Concurrent games** (Gauntlet, Golf) give every goblin (or challenge pair) a run of their own, up to 12 Gauntlet runners and 3 golf tees at once.
- **A heat**: lobby → countdown (3 s, everyone placed and held) → running → results (5 s) → closed. A time game ends when everyone is done or the limit passes; a points game by its clock. Standings by score, ties share a place. A score counts only if the goblin finished (a time game, and not faster than the game's `MIN_TIME`) or scored above zero (a points game).
- **Leaving is always clean**: LEAVE on the play bar (RESET, or `Backspace`, puts you back at your last checkpoint in the Regatta and the Gauntlet), walking away from a lobby, dying or resetting, disconnecting, a spectate, or the goblin's raid setting off. **The raid always wins**: `Raid.onDeparting` (set to `Minigames.leaveAll`) runs before signed-up goblins are sent, and a goblin signed up for the raid is warned `RAID_WARN` (15 s) before it leaves. A heat with nobody left in it ends. Each game's `drop` hook cleans up that goblin's things (their tub, their launcher, their chest).
- **Telling the clients**: every session publishes one JSON `StringValue` in `ReplicatedStorage.LootGoblinsPlay` (state, clocks, roster, scores, the game's own extras), at most four times a second; games that move a lot add a faster `<id>.live` value (the Derby's pets, the crabs). Moving targets (Toss baskets, Gallery ships, the Regatta's cannons) are **functions of the server clock** in `PortGames`, so every client draws them where the server judges them with nothing sent but the clock, and hits are judged by an analytic flight (`PortGames.shotHit`), not physics.
- **Inputs** are rate-limited (`INPUT_RATE`, 12 a second) and clamped by the server: the golf cannon's yaw and power, a throw's pitch and yaw, the gallery's aim. The client never says what it hit.
- **Rewards** go through `Progress.onPortGame` (`Minigames.reward`): see the reward budget below. Everyone in the heat gets their own result card (`PlayResult`: medal, place, best, Shinies, and AGAIN / REMATCH).

### The seven games

| Game | Where (from the Port's centre) | How it plays | Score, medals |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ⛵ **Tiny Boat Regatta** (`server/Regatta.lua`) | The Regatta dock, east | Up to 8 goblins in **Racing Tubs** (`Config.BOAT_TYPES.racer`: a small, light boat on the normal boat controls; the Port lends it, nobody owns one) race one lap of the water round the island through 13 checkpoints (swept, so a fast boat between two ticks still counts). On the way: barrels, bumper buoys, a ramp over a reef, splash cannons that throw every tub inside a warning ring, and **the Teeth**: a rock wall with a narrow channel through it (the shortcut) and a longer safe way round. Out of your tub for 2.5 s: back at your last checkpoint, seated. | Time; gold 36 s, silver 43, bronze 54 (first guesses). Feeds the weekly FASTEST REGATTA board |
| 🪝 **Grapple Gauntlet** (`server/Gauntlet.lua`) | North-west, over the water | A course in the air: bounce pads, swing hooks (V13.2's swing, `F`), a beam and a zipline, eight platforms to a bell. Falling to the water puts you back on the last platform reached (the clock runs on). Everyone runs their own course at once. | Time; gold 40 s, silver 55, bronze 80. Feeds the monthly FASTEST GAUNTLET board |
| ⛳ **Cannon Golf** (`server/CannonGolf.lua`, client `PlayGolf.lua`) | The golf jetty, south-west | Three tee cannons on a jetty and three floating greens (THE PUDDLE, THE SANDBAR, THE LONG ONE). Aim the way you look (within 70° of the tee), **hold to charge** (click, `Space`, gamepad `A`, touch HOLD), let go to be fired by V8's real flight (`Flight.launch`, launcher kind `golf`). Where you land scores: cup 100, so close 70, green 45, fringe 20, splash 0. | Points out of 300; gold 200, silver 120, bronze 50. Feeds the weekly CANNON GOLF board |
| 🐾 **Pet Derby** (`server/PetDerby.lua`, client `PlayCritters.lua`) | The oval, south of the town | Your pet out (or a loaned crab) races round an oval with six hurdles against other goblins' pets and menagerie bots (at least four runners). **CHEER** (`Space`, `E`, click, gamepad `A`, touch CHEER!) as your pet reaches a hurdle: just right is a jump and a burst; too soon, too late or mashing is a tumble. Every pet runs at the same speed (rarity is never speed), and every pet stops once to sniff a flower. | Time; places. Winning counts toward the Derby Laurel pet hat |
| 💰 **Treasure Toss** (`server/TreasureToss.lua`, client `PlayRange.lua`) | Booths east of the square | 40 s to throw chests (aim with the camera; click, `Q`, gamepad `R2`/`L1`, touch THROW) into sliding barrels, a rowboat, a parrot's swinging perch, and the Goblin King, who only eats with his mouth open. A chest must come down into a basket, not up through it. | Points; gold 40, silver 22, bronze 8 |
| 💥 **Target Ship Gallery** (`server/TargetGallery.lua`, client `PlayRange.lua`) | The gallery pier, north-east | Four shore cannons and a cut-out pirate fleet sailing to and fro (a galleon, sloops, a skiff, a kraken, a barge); a hit ship keels over and comes back up. Small, fast ships score more. Aim with the camera; click, `Space`, gamepad `R2`/`A`, touch FIRE. 45 s. | Points; gold 36, silver 20, bronze 8 |
| 🦀 **Crab Chaos** (`server/CrabChaos.lua`, client `PlayCritters.lua`) | The beach, south-west | A crate bursts and 16 crabs (2 golden, worth 3) scatter round a fenced beach. Run into them to catch them; they flee, zigzag and, cornered, burrow and pop up elsewhere. Slower than any running goblin but quick to turn: the dash helps, and herding them together helps more. **Catch every crab before the end and everyone in the round scores 5 more** (the co-operative goal). 45 s. | Points; gold 8, silver 5, bronze 2 |

Every venue is inside the Port's zone and keeps the town's palms off its ground (`PortGames.KEEP_CLEAR`). The play bar (client `PlayHud`) shows the game's icon, a short hint, the clock or countdown, a live roster and LEAVE; while a goblin plays, the Port's sign, sign-up row and next-raid card hide. A venue's moving parts are drawn only within `VENUE_DRAW` (320 studs) of the camera.

### The Captain's Quest Board (`shared/Seasons.lua`, `server/Quests.lua`, client `PortBoard.lua`, `Config.QUESTS`)

- **Three daily and three weekly quests, the same for everyone that day** (so friends can do them together), one per slot: raids, Port games, everything else. Daily rewards 12 / 18 / 25 Shinies by tier, weekly 50 / 75 / 100. Claiming **all three weekly quests** also gives that week's cosmetic in turn (the Quest Pennant flag, the Voyager livery, the Prize Rosette pet hat), or 60 Shinies once it is owned.
- **Pools**: daily: bank in 2 raids, steal 2 treasures, play 3 raids to the end, bank 15 gold, escape a pursuer, finish a Regatta, finish a Gauntlet run, land on 3 golf greens, score 30 in the Toss, catch 8 crabs, hit 10 gallery ships, race a pet, land 3 clean tricks, get thrown about by world chaos twice, play 3 Port games, bank from 2 different boats, play a challenge, snatch treasure from a goblin you knocked down. Weekly: bank in 8 raids, bank 100 gold, escape 3 different island guardians, finish 3 raids in the top 3, finish 5 different Port games, finish 5 Regattas, beat a personal best twice, win 3 gold medals, land 15 tricks, bank from 3 different boats, welcome pets home from 3 expeditions, be thrown about by chaos 8 times. The dealer shuffles each pool per cycle so a quest is never dealt two days running (`questsFor`). No quest needs Robux, a streak, or being online at a time.
- **Resets**: daily at 00:00 UTC, weekly on Monday 00:00 UTC, shown as a countdown on the board. A goblin's quests roll over the moment anything happens after the reset (and every 30 s while they play); **a finished quest nobody claimed is paid at the reset, never lost** (`QuestRollover`).
- **Progress is the server's own events only** (`Progress.Deed`: a steal, a bank, an escape, a trick, a snatch, a Port game; `Progress.RaidRewarded`: played, banked, top three; `WorldChaos.Tossed`, at most once each 4 s), saved in the profile (persistent through reconnects and server changes). `distinct` quests count different islands, games or boats, not repeats.
- **Where**: the board by the boarding pier (prompt `OpensPanel` `quests`: a panel with a QUESTS page, daily and weekly, and a SEASON page of bests, ranks and boards), the Port screen's 📜 chip, and a line on screen when a quest finishes (`QuestDone`). Claiming is `ShopRequest("questclaim", "day" | "week", index)` and waits until the real profile is open. Every client also writes today's quests and its own progress on the board itself (a SurfaceGui).

### Leaderboards and the Hall of Records (`shared/Seasons.lua`, `server/Leaderboards.lua`, client `PortBoard.lua`, `Config.SEASONS`)

| Board | Period | Score | Tiers (bronze / silver / gold) | Prestige |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| BIGGEST HAUL | week | gold banked in one raid | 10 / 20 / 32 | #1: Haul Champion title; top 10: Leaderboard Pennant |
| PIRATE CHAMPIONSHIP (V13.4, id `crown`) | week | a goblin's best 3 raids of the week added up | 25 / 50 / 80 | #1: Captain of the Week title; top 10: Leaderboard Pennant and Champion's Standard; gold tier: Lucky Doubloon pet hat |
| FASTEST REGATTA | week | one lap, to the hundredth | 54 / 43 / 36 s | #1: Regatta Ace title; top 10: Leaderboard Pennant and Checkered Racer livery; gold tier: Regatta Burgee flag |
| CANNON GOLF | week | best round of three | 50 / 120 / 200 | #1: Cannon Golf Ace title; top 10: Leaderboard Pennant |
| PIRATE LEGENDS (V13.3's monthly PIRATE CHAMPIONSHIP, renamed in V13.4; id `champion` kept) | month | **a goblin's best 5 raids of the month added up** (skill, not hours) | 40 / 80 / 130 | #1: Pirate Champion title; top 10: Championship Contender title and Champion's Sails; gold tier (V13.4): Legend's Gilt sails |
| FASTEST GAUNTLET | month | one run | 80 / 55 / 40 s | #1: Gauntlet Legend title |

- **Shinies**: a tier pays 10 / 20 / 35 a weekly board and 25 / 50 / 80 a monthly one, whatever anyone else did (so an ordinary goblin earns something every week); a placement adds 100 (#1), 60 (top 3), 40 (top 10), 15 (top 100) weekly and 250 / 150 / 80 / 30 monthly. Cosmetics are prestige only (titles, pennants, sails, pet hats: `rarity = "season"`, never sold).
- **Scores are the server's own measurements only** (a raid's banked gold from `Raid.finish` through `Progress`, a lap or round timed by the server's games; times faster than a game's `MIN_TIME` are refused). A goblin's best per board and period is saved in their profile first (`Seasons.submit`), then written to the board's OrderedDataStore (`LG_Board_<board>`, scope = the period key: `w<index>` or `m<YYYY-MM>`) with `UpdateAsync` keeping only the better value, at most once per `WRITE_GAP` (20 s) per board, and again whenever their profile opens (a crash never loses a place for long).
- **Reading**: each board's top 100 is read every `REFRESH` (120 s); the top 10 and last period's top three go on the Hall of Records (workspace attribute `Board_<id>`), names from `UserService`; **friends** in the top rows are marked (`IsFriendsWith`, client side). A goblin's own bests and ranks are the player attribute `Season`.
- **Season end**: once a period has been over `SETTLE` (15 min), the first server to notice writes its final standings (the top 100) to `LG_Hall_v1` with one `UpdateAsync` that never replaces a final record; every server then reads the same standings: **the durable record of who won**. **Rewards are paid into each goblin's own profile, once** (`Seasons.pay` marks the period paid in the same profile change), whenever they are next in a server: offline at the reset loses nothing. If the standings never appear (14 days), the tier is still paid, without a placement. Trophies (`SeasonReward`) are kept in the profile (`season.trophies`, at most 24) and shown in the sanctuary's trophy case.
- **Calendar**: UTC days, Monday weeks, calendar months (`Seasons.period`, `bounds`, `key`; checked against 41,000 days of a reference calendar).
- In Studio without API access the stores are in-memory stand-ins (everything resets when Play stops).

### The pet sanctuary and expeditions (`shared/Habitat.lua`, `server/Sanctuary.lua`, client `Sanctuary.lua`, `PetCrowd.lua`, `Config.PET_ISLES`, `Config.EXPEDITIONS`)

- **An isle for every goblin in the server**, floating in two rings over the town (32 isles), built from their profile when it opens. The **Pet Sanctuary Lift** (a balloon basket by the square) takes you up to your own (`E`) or to anyone's (VISIT); the Port screen's 🐾 chip does too; a hop from the edge lands you back in the Port (no fall damage there). Each isle has its owner's name, a basket back down, a pond, nests, lights, an expedition dock, four decoration spots and a trophy case.
- **The pets**: up to 12 of the pets a goblin owns live there (their choice, or the one out first and then the newest), drawn by every client near the isle with V11's shared animator (`PetLook`, through `PetCrowd`, moved with `BulkMoveTo`, animated only within `DRAW`, 240 studs). They wander, rest, sniff and do their idle quirks. **Anyone on the isle** can FEED them (they come running to the bowl), throw a BALL (they chase it to where you look) and ring the BELL (they all come running to it); each is a few seconds apart for the whole isle.
- **Decorating, modestly** (all Shinies, bought once): five themes (Meadow free; Beach Cove 150, Blossom Garden 220, Crystal Grotto 300, Haunted Grove 300), a pond (Puddle → Lily Pond 120 → Lagoon & Fountain 260), nests (90, 200), lights (80, 180), the expedition dock (Rowboat: 1 expedition → Sloop 220: 2 → Little Galleon 480: 3), and eight decorations for four spots (Flower Bed 30 to Your Statue 150, a mannequin dressed in your look). Only the dock changes anything: how many expeditions run at once.
- **Pet expeditions**: send an owned pet on the Shore Scavenge (2 h, 6 Shinies), the Reef Run (6 h, 12) or the Long Voyage (12 h, 20). It comes back on the server's clock (`os.time`), online or not, and is collected once (collecting removes it in the same profile change that pays it). **At most 30 Shinies a UTC day, whatever the pets** (a full day of expeditions is well under one hour of raids); every pet earns the same; nothing is sold for Robux. A pet away is not on the isle and cannot be worn (sending your worn pet takes it off); it can be called home early for nothing.
- **Actions** (`ShopRequest`, real profile open first): `sanctbuy(kind, id)`, `sanctplace(socket, decor)`, `sancttheme(theme)`, `residents(list)`, `expsend(pet, trip)`, `expcollect(id)`, `exprecall(id)`. Movement and interactions: `SanctuaryRequest("home" | "visit", userId | "port" | "feed" | "toy" | "bell")`.

### Challenges (`server/Challenges.lua`, client `Challenge.lua`, `Config.CHALLENGES`)

- **Ask** any goblin in the Port to any of the seven games from the ⚔ chip (a picker of goblins and games). Both must be in the Port, free and not playing; one invitation out at a time, 3 s between asks. The other sees ACCEPT / NO THANKS for 20 s; the asker can take it back; silence is a no; leaving cancels it.
- **The heat** is a private session at the venue, started at once or, if the venue is busy, right after the heat on it (no second server, no matchmaking). If one of them leaves while it waits, it is called off.
- **Result**: the better score wins; a time game needs a finish; equal is a TIE. Leaving or disconnecting is a FORFEIT: the other is told they won, but **a forfeit pays nothing** (nobody farms an opponent who walks off). A win pays 4 Shinies and a tie 2, at most 5 paid a day and 2 against the same goblin (counters in the profile). Wins count toward The Challenger title (5 wins). **REMATCH** on the result card: when both press it within 15 s, the same game again.

### What's next after a raid (`server/Prospects.lua`, client `NextUp.lua`)

As a goblin comes home, a compact card (on the left under the next raid's chaos card; it never blocks anything, slides away by itself, × closes it, and it goes when the next raid starts) shows: the Shinies that raid paid and the balance; up to two quests that moved (finished ones first: claim them at the board); **a goal** (the dearest boat they can afford now, or the nearest boat or pet to save for and about how many raids away); records (best haul this week, a place on a board, the Championship so far); one suggested Port game (one a quest wants, one never tried, or a best to beat), with SHOW ME, which points the way to its venue; and the next raid's world chaos. The Port screen keeps a one-line goal under the sign.

### Titles (`Catalog` slot `title`, `shared/StyleFx.lua` `TITLES`, client `Titles.lua`)

A new wearable slot: a short line over a goblin's head (billboard, drawn by each client from `Look`). Four are bought (Landlubber 30, Scallywag 60, Old Sea Dog 120, Goblin Royalty 400), three are trophies (Port Regular: try all seven games; Quest Taker: claim 10 quests; The Challenger: win 5 challenges), six are season prizes. They are worn in the wardrobe like any item (and saved in outfit presets).

### The reward budget (economy integration)

Raids stay the main way to earn: a typical raid pays about 24 Shinies in 7.3 minutes, about 196 an hour (`Config.PROGRESS`, unchanged; `EconomySpec`). Everything V13.3 adds is small and **capped per goblin per UTC day in the saved profile**, so leaving, rejoining or changing servers resets nothing:

| Source | Pays | Cap |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Port games | 1 a finished run, +1/+2/+4 bronze/silver/gold, +1 for winning a heat of two or more humans, +2 for a personal best (not the first score) | 6 paid runs per game a day, 40 Shinies a day, 3 best bonuses a day; runs after that still count for bests, quests and boards |
| Daily quests | 12 / 18 / 25 | three a day (about 55 if all are done) |
| Weekly quests | 50 / 75 / 100, and the week's cosmetic (or 60) for all three | three a week |
| Leaderboards | tiers 10 to 35 a weekly board, 25 to 80 a monthly; placements 15 to 250 | once per board and period, paid into the profile |
| Expeditions | 6 / 12 / 20 a trip | 30 a day, whatever the pets |
| Challenges | 4 a win, 2 a tie, forfeits nothing | 5 paid a day, 2 against the same goblin |
| Achievements | V11/V13's, plus the V13.3 trophies (Port Regular, First Voyage, Seasoned Explorers, Quest Taker, The Challenger, Derby Winner) | once ever |

Expected earnings a day (first estimates from the numbers above, not measurements):

| | Casual (about 30 min) | Active (about 2 h) | Skilled (about 2 h, wins medals and places on boards) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Raids | ~96 (4 raids) | ~336 (14 raids) | ~400 (14 bigger raids) |
| Port games | ~10 | 40 (cap) | 40 (cap) |
| Daily quests | ~30 (two of three) | ~55 | ~55 |
| Weekly quests, per day | ~5 | ~35 | ~40 |
| Expeditions | ~12 | 30 (cap) | 30 (cap) |
| Leaderboards, per day | ~2 (a bronze tier) | ~9 (tiers) | ~45 (gold tiers, top 10s) |
| Challenges | 0 | ~5 | ~20 |
| **Total** | **~155 (raids ~62%)** | **~510 (raids ~66%)** | **~630 (raids ~63%)** |

A boat (350 to 700) is therefore 3 to 5 casual days or about a day of active play, as before V13.3 plus a little. **Anti-farming**: per-goblin daily caps saved in the profile; no reward for standing about (a points score above zero, a time game finished and not faster than `MIN_TIME`); the heat winner's bonus needs two or more humans; challenge forfeits pay nothing and pairs are capped; leaderboard scores are measured by the server; season rewards are marked paid in the same profile change; expeditions are removed from the profile when collected. A second account earns only its own capped amounts and cannot give them to the first (there is no trading).

### Persistence (`server/ProfileSchema.lua` version 4)
