## Report: 2026-10-22-v13-3-living-port.md

# V13.3: The Living Port (2026-10-22)

Ninety's brief: a playtester enjoyed the raids but was not moved to keep playing past a round or two, so give goblins reasons to play another five minutes, another raid and another day, through active novelty, progression, social competition and collecting, without chores. Built by Claude Opus 5.5 on branch `feature/v13-3-living-port`, from `main` at `859f35e` (V13.2, Sea of Chaos, merged through PRs #24 to #27). **The PR is not merged**, as the brief asked.

**Read this first.** As the brief asked, **nobody played V13.3 to build it**: no AI playthroughs, no screenshots, no simulated controls, no debug hooks. It was validated by code review, StyLua and Selene, both Rojo builds, **136 automated Luau tests** run in Studio's Edit mode, and **one start of Play to read the console** (empty of errors on server and client), stopped at once. Every game, panel and board below is therefore **unplayed**: whether it works in the hands of a person, reads at a glance and is fun is the team's checklist in section 9. The full description is `docs/GAME_DESIGN.md`, **V13.3: The Living Port**.

## 1. What was built

| Deliverable | Where | In short |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Seven Port games | `server/Minigames.lua` (framework), `Regatta`, `Gauntlet`, `CannonGolf`, `PetDerby`, `TreasureToss`, `TargetGallery`, `CrabChaos`; `shared/PortGames.lua`; client `PlayHud`, `PlayGolf`, `PlayRange`, `PlayCritters` | One framework (lobby, countdown, standings, leaving, results, rewards, publishing) and seven small modules on the game's own systems: real boats (a new Racing Tub class the Port lends), V13.2's swing, V8's flight launchers, V11's pet animator, the cannons' ballistics |
| Captain's Quest Board | `shared/Seasons.lua`, `server/Quests.lua`, client `PortBoard` | 3 daily + 3 weekly quests, the same for everyone, from pools of 18 and 12; UTC resets; unclaimed finished quests paid at the reset; a weekly cosmetic for all three |
| Leaderboards | `shared/Seasons.lua`, `server/Leaderboards.lua`, client `PortBoard` | Weekly: Biggest Haul, Fastest Regatta, Cannon Golf. Monthly: the Pirate Championship (best 5 raids), Fastest Gauntlet. OrderedDataStores per period, a durable Hall of final standings, tier + placement rewards paid once into each profile |
| Pet sanctuary | `shared/Habitat.lua`, `server/Sanctuary.lua`, client `Sanctuary`, `PetCrowd` | A floating isle per goblin (32), up to 12 owned pets living there, feed / ball / bell for anyone on the isle, themes, upgrades, decorations, visiting |
| Pet expeditions | the same | 2 h / 6 h / 12 h trips for 6 / 12 / 20 Shinies, server clock, offline progress, collected once, at most 30 a day whatever the pets |
| Social challenges | `server/Challenges.lua`, client `Challenge` | Invite any goblin in the Port to any game; accept, decline, cancel, expiry, disconnect, ties, forfeits, rewards with caps, rematch; private heats at the existing venues |
| After the raid | `server/Prospects.lua`, client `NextUp` | A compact, non-blocking card: Shinies, quests that moved, the boat or pet to buy or save for, records and ranks, one suggested game, the next chaos |
| Economy | `Config.PLAYGROUND`, `QUESTS`, `SEASONS`, `EXPEDITIONS`, `CHALLENGES`; `Progress.onPortGame` | All Shinies, all capped per goblin per UTC day in the profile; the budget and the casual / active / skilled table are in GAME_DESIGN.md |
| Cosmetics | `shared/Catalog.lua`, `StyleFx`, `BoatLook`, `PetLook`, client `Titles` | A new **title** slot (shown over the head) and 22 items: 4 bought titles, 3 trophy titles, 6 season titles, 3 flags, 3 liveries, 3 pet hats; 6 new achievements |
| Persistence | `server/ProfileSchema.lua` v4, `Economy.mergePort` | Profile version 4 with V13.3 tables, migration from v2 and v3, repair of damaged tables |
| Retention instrumentation | `server/Analytics.lua`, `Progress` | 7 once-ever milestones, a per-session RaidContinuation funnel, return and session events, economy SKUs per source |

## 2. How it fits the game

- **Isolation from raids.** The raid always wins: `Raid.onDeparting` ends a goblin's Port game before they are sent (and a goblin signed up is warned 15 s before), a goblin whose `Zone` becomes `raid` or who starts watching leaves their game, Port boats (`Boats.spawnPortBoat`) and Port launchers are left alone by the raid's resets, and every venue is inside the Port's zone. Nothing in V13.3 runs during a raid except quest and leaderboard bookkeeping on the server's own raid events.
- **Server authority.** Scores, times, hits and catches are the server's measurements; moving targets are functions of the server clock shared with the clients (`PortGames`), and hits are judged analytically (`PortGames.shotHit`), so nothing the client says about a hit is believed. Inputs are rate-limited and clamped. Every Shiny is paid by `Progress` with its cap in the profile. Known gaps (the Regatta tub and a running goblin move on their own clients) are written in GAME_DESIGN.md, "Who decides what".
- **Per-frame work.** One Heartbeat (`Minigames.tick`) only for running sessions; the games tick their own simulations at 10 to 20 Hz (crabs, the Derby, Regatta checkpoints); publishing is change-only and at most four times a second; clients draw venues within 320 studs and isle pets within 240, with `BulkMoveTo`.
- **Input.** Every game's action has a keyboard key, a gamepad button and a touch button (ContextActionService), and the panels are V11's `Ui` kit (mouse, touch, gamepad selection). None of it has been tried on a phone or a controller.
- **Robux.** Nothing new is sold for Robux and no product id was invented; everything is Shinies or earned.

## 3. Economy (summary)

Raids stay the main earner: a typical raid pays about 24 Shinies in 7.3 minutes (unchanged). Expected per day: **casual ~155 (raids ~62%), active ~510 (~66%), skilled ~630 (~63%)**. Caps: Port games 40 a day (6 paid runs per game, 3 best bonuses), daily quests ~55, weekly quests 50 to 100 each, expeditions 30, challenges 5 paid wins (2 per opponent, forfeits pay nothing), leaderboards once per period. Restarts, rejoining and switching servers cannot farm (caps are in the profile); alternate accounts earn only their own capped amounts and cannot pass them on (no trading). Full table: GAME_DESIGN.md, "The reward budget".

## 4. Persistence and migration

Profile version 4 (`ProfileSchema.VERSION`). A v2 or v3 profile upgrades keeping every item, Shiny, stat and achievement, with empty V13.3 tables; damaged V13.3 tables are repaired; a newer version is never opened or written (unchanged rule). Earnings made while a profile was locked by another server merge across once, V13.3 counters included. Season rewards are marked paid in the same profile change that pays them; expeditions are removed in the same change that pays them; the Hall's final record is written with an `UpdateAsync` that never replaces a final one. Tests: `PersistenceSpec` (v3 → v4, damaged v4), `SeasonsSpec` (paid once, trimmed only after paid), `HabitatSpec` (paid once, daily cap).

## 5. Retention instrumentation

Milestones once per goblin ever: `FirstRaidCompleted`, `SecondRaidStarted`, `SecondRaidCompleted`, `FirstMinigamePlayed`, `FirstQuestCompleted`, `FirstExpeditionCollected`, `FirstSpecialtyBoat`. A `RaidContinuation` funnel per play session (raid finished → next raid joined → next raid finished): **its step 1 → 2 conversion is the brief's most important question**, whether a goblin who finishes a raid chooses another (raids are opt-in since V13.2, so it is always a choice). Also `RaidJoined`, `SessionSummary`, `ReturnSession`, `PortGamePlayed`, `QuestClaimed`, `ChallengePlayed`, and economy SKUs per source. How to read them in the Creator Hub: GAME_DESIGN.md, "Retention instrumentation". **There is no data yet, and nothing here claims V13.3 improves retention.**

## 6. Tests and checks

- **StyLua** `--check`: clean. **Selene**: 0 errors, 0 warnings. **Rojo**: the game place and the test place both build.
- **Luau tests: 136 passed, 0 failed** (Studio Edit mode; the place's scripts were made identical to the files on disk first, and every module replaced with a fresh copy so no cached code ran). New: `SeasonsSpec` (10: the calendar against a reference over 41,000 days, the quest dealer never repeating a quest next day, progress and claiming once, unclaimed quests paid at the reset, distinct quests, the weekly cosmetic in turn, board scores only improving with times in hundredths, the Championship's best five, a period paid once by tier and rank, every season cosmetic earnable, records trimmed only after paid), `PortGamesSpec` (11: every venue inside the Port with a medal ladder, run rewards and the first score not being a "best", daily caps resetting tomorrow, swept checkpoints, the Regatta's 13 checkpoints and the Teeth, the Gauntlet's platforms in order and within reach of each other, golf power and aim limits and the far green in reach, fair Derby lanes and judge window, toss baskets scoring only on the way down, the gallery's ball landing where aimed, every range target in front of its booth), `HabitatSpec` (5: buying once and in order, residents owned and capped, expeditions on the server clock paid once, the daily cap whatever the pets, passive income well under a raid hour), plus 2 `PersistenceSpec` and 1 `CatalogSpec` case. V13.2's 107 all still pass.
- **One boot check**: Play started once to read the console: server and client logs empty of errors (one Roblox avatar-asset warning that is not the game's); the quest board, the Hall of Records, the lift, all seven venues and every V13.3 screen were created; the boards published this week's and last period's standings (in-memory stores). Play stopped.
- **Not run**: any game, panel, quest, challenge, isle or reward by hand; a second player; a phone or controller; real DataStores (Studio has no API access here), so no live leaderboard, Hall or season payment.

## 7. Bugs found and fixed before anyone played

- **The pet isles' settings replaced V9's sanctuary.** They were first named `Config.SANCTUARY`, which already held the safe water round Goblin Cove (`RADIUS`, `BUOYS`): pursuits, the sea-run buoys, the map and the minimap would have errored in every raid. `ChaosSpec` caught it; the isles' table is now `Config.PET_ISLES`.
- **The specialty-boat milestone was never sent**: now sent on buying a boat that is not free and after any Robux grant that brings one.
- Found while building, by review and the new tests: the quest dealer could deal the same quest two days running (now a per-cycle shuffle); a quest reset inside a claim could lose the week's cosmetic (the reset's payout is now settled wherever it happens); a 32-bit hash overflowed Luau's exact integers (split multiplication); waiting challenge sessions counted as running heats and could block a venue; the Regatta's reef could be ridden over; a client drew range targets rotated wrongly; the golf tee's cannon would have answered the skyship's controls; a challenge record that never started was never forgotten.

## 8. Instructions this brief superseded

The brief asked that earlier instructions requiring exhaustive Studio playtesting be identified, not silently changed. They are **AGENTS.md, "Tools and validation"** ("...capture visual results, and playtest gameplay changes") and **docs/GAME_DESIGN.md, "Testing expectations"** ("Gameplay changes also need a Studio playtest with an empty console"). For V13.3 the brief replaced them with code inspection, lint, builds and automated tests; neither was edited (GAME_DESIGN.md only notes the V13.3 exception beside the rule). Studio was opened once, through `./scripts/dev.ps1 -OpenStudio`, for the Luau tests and the boot check; that window is still open, in Edit mode.

## 9. Human playtest checklist (three people, about 45 minutes)

Start: double-click **Play Loot Goblins**, then in Studio **Test > Server & Clients > 3 players > Play**. In the Port press `H` to see what is where. Saving does not persist in Studio (it resets when Play stops), so test saving and the weekly reset only in a published test place with **Enable Studio Access to API Services** on.

1. **First look (1 min each).** Without the help card, can you find the seven games, the Quest Board and the pink balloon lift? Do the signs say what each game is?
2. **Every game once** (each player picks two or three; do them together where you can):
   - **Regatta**: all three race. Is a lap about 30 to 45 s? Does anyone dare the gap in the Teeth? Is being thrown by a splash cannon funny or unfair? Does RESET (`Backspace`) put you back sensibly?
   - **Gauntlet**: can everyone finish? Is falling back to the last platform fair? Too hard or too easy?
   - **Cannon Golf**: can you reach the far green? Is hold-to-charge clear? Do your landings score where they look like they should?
   - **Pet Derby**: does cheering feel like timing, not luck? Does it make you laugh?
   - **Treasure Toss** and **Target Gallery**: do hits count when they look like hits? Is the King's mouth readable?
   - **Crab Chaos**: can the three of you catch every crab (the team bonus)? Is chasing crabs fun or annoying?
3. **Leaving.** In any game: press LEAVE; walk away during the lobby; join the raid while playing (the game should warn you 15 s before the raid leaves, then end); reset your character. Nothing should get stuck (a frozen goblin, a game that never ends, a sign stuck on "busy").
4. **Quests.** Open the board. Is every quest clear? Do one daily quest from a Port game and one from a raid, and claim them. Did a finished quest show on screen when it finished?
5. **After a raid.** Play a raid, come home: does the what's-next card show something you actually wanted to do next? Was it in the way? Did you want to play another raid?
6. **Challenges.** Challenge each other from the ⚔ chip: say no once, let one expire, accept one, leave halfway through one (the other should be told they won), and press REMATCH after one.
7. **Sanctuary.** Ride the lift. Are your pets there? Feed them, throw the ball, ring the bell. Visit each other's isles. Buy a cheap decoration and place it. Send a pet on the Shore Scavenge (2 h); in a published place, come back later and collect it.
8. **Leaderboards.** After a Regatta, a golf round and a raid with gold, do your scores appear on the Hall of Records within about two minutes? Are friends marked?
9. **Feel.** Is the Port lively or a wall of menus? Is anything on screen too wordy? Any stutter with three goblins and their pets out?
10. **If you can**: a phone or a controller in one game each.

**How to report**: say what felt bad or confusing, and send a screenshot of any red error (View > Output). Numbers you think are wrong (a medal time, a price, a reward) are easy to change; name the game and the number.

## 10. Not tested, risks and first guesses

- **Every number is a first guess**, the course times above all: medal times for the Regatta (36 / 43 / 54 s) and the Gauntlet (40 / 55 / 80 s) come from distances and speeds, not from anyone racing. The Gauntlet's gaps were checked geometrically (`PortGamesSpec`), not by a goblin jumping them.
- **Live DataStores** (boards, the Hall, season payments) ran only against in-memory stand-ins. Their request budgets were sized for a full server (a board read every 2 min, a write per board per goblin at most every 20 s) but never measured.
- **Two or more players**: heats, queues, challenges, visiting, ties and forfeits were exercised only by the code's own rules and tests.
- **Client-moved things**: a modified client could drive a Regatta tub faster or cut Gauntlet corners within limits (both written down as known gaps).
- **Isles** are rebuilt whenever their look changes; with 32 goblins decorating at once that is a burst of parts. More than 32 goblins: the extras get no isle.

## Report: 2026-10-19-v13-2-sea-of-chaos.md

# V13.2: Sea of Chaos (2026-10-19)

Ninety's brief: make encounters more frequent, movement more expressive, boats more balanced and every raid more unpredictable, without making the game simply harder. Built by Claude Opus 5.5 on branch `feature/v13-2-sea-of-chaos`, stacked on V13.1 (`fix/v13-playtest-feedback`, PR #25), which was stacked on V13 (`feature/v13-goblin-port`, PR #24).

**Status (2026-10-22):** merged into `main` through PRs [#24](https://github.com/EnrikR2002/Loot-Goblins/pull/24), [#25](https://github.com/EnrikR2002/Loot-Goblins/pull/25) and [#26](https://github.com/EnrikR2002/Loot-Goblins/pull/26). The team has since tested V13.2 in play; that feedback is not yet recorded in this report.

**Read this first.** Everything below was built and tested by one AI on **one** Roblox Studio client, through a Studio-only test hook (a Workspace script obeying a `DebugCmd` attribute; never committed) and real key presses and clicks where it says so. At the time of this report nobody had played V13.2. It has never had a second player, a phone or a real controller. Travel times come from server-driven test boats following the sea's own pathfinder, not from people. **Passing tests and smooth numbers do not prove the boats are balanced or the chaos is fun**: that needs Ninety, Ethan and Enrik playing it together.

![The Port before a raid: WAITING FOR RAIDERS, the next raid's chaos and route on the left, JOIN NEXT RAID](2026-10-19-v13-2-port-waiting.jpg)

## 1. What changed

| Brief | Now |
| --- | --- |
| §3 On foot: momentum, grapple first | **No sprint key.** Running builds speed by itself: 21 on the first step, the normal 28 after 0.3 s, **38 after about 2 s**; a sharp turn or stopping spends it, jumps, falls, swings and landings keep it. **The grapple swings**: hook anything above you (rock, tree, bridge, mast, a moving boat) and you swing on a pendulum, `W A S D` pump, hold `F` to reel in, `F` or `Space` lets go keeping the speed. **Dash** stays as the dodge and quick start (`Shift` or `C`). The PvP catch is now a **thrown hook** you can see and dash out of. Poltergoblin stays switched off |
| §4 Rebalance boats | Cruise speeds compressed from **96–135 to 106–118**, acceleration from **54–100 to 61–72**, boost ×1.5 → ×1.42, Nitro ×1.75 → ×1.45. Measured: from Skull Rock the fleet now docks within **3.5 s** of each other (was 11.2 s) |
| §5 Ten classes | **Anchorjack** (the anchor, now only on this boat), **Wavebreaker** (a ring of water), **Corsair** (boarding hook) added; every class's `R` escapes, disrupts, or both. Skiff and Cutter free; the other eight for Shinies (350–700), with inert Robux keys |
| §6 Cannon on every boat | **Click while driving fires the bow gun** (gamepad `R2`, touch GUN): 2.2 s reload, 240 studs, ±70° off the bow, shoves and splashes, never sinks a boat or knocks treasure loose, never in the Port or at home |
| §7 Skyship | It **flies one of seven routes** (forwards or backwards) across the sea; cannons reach about **1,200 studs**, so what you can reach changes as it flies. **10 s prep with the cannons locked by the server**, then a 32 s pass; the six-minute clock starts after it. All 110 route-and-island landings verified dry |
| §8 Opt-in | **Nobody is sent on a raid they did not join.** JOIN NEXT RAID (or walk aboard the Little Goblin), cancel any time before it leaves, AUTO-JOIN for regulars; no empty raids; late join and spectating as before; **LEAVE THIS RAID** (two presses) goes home, forfeiting that raid's gold and Shinies |
| §9 World chaos | **One of eight events per raid**, named with its icon in the Port before anyone picks a boat: Meteor Mayhem, Kraken's Tantrum, Rogue Wave Rampage, Cannonball Crossfire, Barrel Apocalypse, Whirlpool Outbreak, Haunted Seas, Thunderstruck. Telegraphed episodes near goblins, each drawn differently, with calm between |

## 2. On foot

**Momentum** (`shared/Momentum.lua`, played by the goblin's own client over the server's speed cap; `Config.MOMENTUM`). Measured with a real `W` held on Tangle Isle:

| Time running | 0.5 s | 0.6 s | 1.0 s | 1.6 s | 2.1 s | 2.5 s on |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Speed (studs/s) | 23 | 27 | 29 | 32 | 36 | **38** |

A full reverse (`S`) dropped it to 28 and it built again; stopping returns to 21. A carrier's top is 29 to 37 (weight). The server still sets the base speed (`Movement`'s MoveCap: carrying, water, a knockout) and the goblin's own client multiplies it. As with every Roblox character the client moves its own body: there is no server check on running speed, before V13.2 or now (a known limit, not new).

**The swing** (`shared/Swing.lua`, `Config.SWING`): the aim finds a hook within 170 studs with a forgiving 7° cone. Above you by 6 studs or more it is a **swing** (gravity 150, pump 46 studs/s², top 125 studs/s on the rope, 7 s at most); level or below it is V7's straight **pull**. Speed carried off a rope (up to 92) slides back to the run 0.75 s after landing. A hook on a boat seats you (V7). Carriers can swing too, every 2.4 s (was 5).

Measured (real `F`, `W`, `Space` on Tangle Isle's canopy bridge, 42 studs up): hooked from standing, at the rope's cap (125) within about 0.3 s, about 95 studs covered in 0.8 s; released, landed at full momentum (38). One run flew straight into a tree trunk in its path, which is the kind of thing a human must judge: **it is fast, and possibly too fast**.

**The catch** is a thrown hook (170 studs/s, 7 studs wide) instead of an instant hit: a carrier who sees it coming can dash out of its line. Shell Tortoise pets still bounce one catch; Spring Frog still speeds the dash; Pocket Ghost (SPIRIT) still shortens a knockout.

![Swinging from the Tangle's canopy bridge](2026-10-19-v13-2-grapple-swing.jpg)

## 3. Boats: before and after

V13.1's numbers (git `8972cb4`) against V13.2's (`Config.BOAT_TYPES`):

| Class | Top speed | Acceleration | Turn | Hull |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Skiff | 135 → **118** | 100 → **72** | 2.5 → 2.6 | 160 → 170 |
| Cutter | 110 → **114** | 72 → **69** | 1.8 → 1.9 | 420 |
| Reefhopper | 124 → **113** | 92 → **70** | 2.4 → 2.45 | 150 → 160 |
| Broadside | 98 → **108** | 58 → **63** | 1.45 → 1.5 | 520 |
| Stormrunner | 122 → **112** (132 in a storm) | 84 → **67** | 2.1 → 2.15 | 260 → 270 |
| Wraith | 128 → **115** | 96 → **71** | 3.1 | 120 → 130 |
| Ironbelly | 96 → **106** | 54 → **61** | 1.35 → 1.4 | 640 |
| Anchorjack (new) | **110** | **65** | 2.2 | 360 |
| Wavebreaker (new) | **111** | **66** | 2.0 | 320 |
| Corsair (new) | **116** | **68** | 2.3 | 250 |
| Patrol ship (Navy) | 106 → 104 | 68 → 64 | | |

Shared: boost ×1.5 → **×1.42** (a Skiff 168, an Ironbelly 150), boost thrust 2.4 → 2.2, the standstill punch 0.9 → 0.6, super jump from 150 → **132** (still above every cruise, below every boost) to 188 for the full height. Nitro ×1.75 → **×1.45** for 1.1 s (was 1.3), kick 30 → 18, cooldown 15 s: its worth is now **breaking free** (anchors, hooks, tows, whirlpools: shoves are shrugged off while it burns), not winning races.

### Travel times (measured)

Each class driven by the server from the shore of an island to the Hoard's docks (within 260 studs of it), along the path `SeaNav` gives that hull's draft, full throttle, Shift whenever it was ready (with its own cooldown), no abilities, test boats unable to touch each other. "Before" is the same run in the same session with V13.1's numbers patched in for the seven old classes.

| Class | Crystal Isle → docks (1,700 studs) | Tangle Isle → docks (2,700) | Skull Rock → docks (4,330) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Skiff | 10.5 → **12.5** s | 16.4 → **19.4** | 25.8 → **31.3** |
| Cutter | 12.3 → **12.5** | 20.6 → **19.3** | 31.5 → **31.3** |
| Reefhopper | 11.4 → **13.2** | 18.1 → **20.5** | 28.6 → **32.5** |
| Broadside | 14.2 → **13.6** | 22.5 → **22.4** | 36.6 → **33.8** |
| Stormrunner | 11.4 → **12.8** | 17.6 → **21.1** | 28.3 → **31.9** |
| Wraith | 10.9 → **12.7** | 17.4 → **19.7** | 26.9 → **31.5** |
| Ironbelly | 14.5 → **13.8** | 23.0 → **22.9** | 37.0 → **34.5** |
| Anchorjack | **13.0** | **21.3** | **32.1** |
| Wavebreaker | **12.9** | **20.5** | **32.0** |
| Corsair | **12.4** | **19.6** | **31.0** |
| **Spread (slowest − fastest)** | 4.0 → **1.4 s** | 6.6 → **3.6 s** | 11.2 → **3.5 s** |

What it says: the Skiff no longer wins by seconds; **the free Cutter keeps pace with it** everywhere; the slow pair (Broadside, Ironbelly) lost most of their penalty; the long Tangle route still favours good turners (it winds). Top speeds seen on the way (boosts and currents) fell from 141–217 to 148–179. A long crossing takes 3 to 6 s longer in the fast boats: that time is now spent near other boats instead of ahead of them.

### The fleet

| Class | Price | Role | Size (W × H × L) | Top | Accel | Turn | Hull | Crash taken | Crew | `R` ability (cooldown) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Skiff | free | Escape artist | 9 × 3 × 20 | 118 | 72 | 2.6 | 170 | ×1.00 | 1 | 🔥 NITRO (15 s): a burst that breaks every chain, hook and tow and shrugs off shoves |
| Cutter | free | All-rounder | 14 × 4 × 34 | 114 | 69 | 1.9 | 420 | ×0.60 | 3 | 📯 RALLY HORN (16 s): every boat within 150 surges, a hull patch, nearby pursuers and the Leviathan flinch |

| Broadside | 700 | Gunboat | 16 × 5 × 38 | 108 | 63 | 1.5 | 520 | ×0.50 | 3 | 💣 BROADSIDE (10 s) |
| Stormrunner | 550 | Storm chaser | 11 × 3.5 × 26 | 112 | 67 | 2.15 | 270 | ×0.85 | 2 | 🌪 TWISTER (24 s, was 28) |
| Wraith | 500 | Phantom | 8 × 2.6 × 22 | 115 | 71 | 3.1 | 130 | ×1.25 | 1 | 👻 PHANTOM (11 s) |
| Ironbelly | 600 | Bruiser | 18 × 6 × 36 | 106 | 61 | 1.4 | 640 | ×0.30 | 4 | 🐗 RAM PLOW (14 s) |
| **Anchorjack** | 500 | Anchor | 13 × 4 × 28 | 110 | 65 | 2.2 | 360 | ×0.70 | 2 | ⚓ ANCHOR (9 s): snag a rival boat ahead (150 studs) and chain it to you for 3.5 s, or bite a rock or the sea bed and swing round it; `R` again lets go as a slingshot |
| **Wavebreaker** | 550 | Wave maker | 14 × 4 × 26 | 111 | 66 | 2.0 | 320 | ×0.75 | 2 | 🌊 BREAKER (11 s): a ring of water 115 studs out throws boats away and washes swimmers back; you hop onto the crest and surge. Rides rogue waves 1.6× farther |

No boat ahead: it zips you to a rock |

Every ability is played by whichever machine simulates the hull and judged by the server (`BoatAbilities`: range, arc, safe zones, cooldown, what the anti-cheat lets the hull do meanwhile). The anchor and the hook name the rival hull the client chose, which the server believes only if it passes the same tests.

### The abilities, measured (real `R` presses, one client, a server-driven rival)

| Ability | What happened |
| --- | --- |
| ⚓ Anchor, snag | Rival Skiff fleeing at 70: **dropped to 6 on the snag**, held on the chain 3.5 s (its speed about halved), the Anchorjack towed along at 50–72; then it broke free. "SNAGGED! R lets the chain go" |
| ⚓ Anchor, swing + sling | At 92, anchor bit the sea bed: **swung 160° in 1.7 s** at about 80, then `R` let go: **79 → 135** (a slingshot hairpin) |
| ⚔ Boarding hook | Hooked a Skiff fleeing at 90 from 107 studs: reeled at up to 158, **BOARDED** ("FrikiEnriki BOARDED a Skiff!"): the rival 24 hull damage, the Corsair 12, the rival knocked 48° off its line and slowed (96 → 84) |
| 🌊 Breaker | Rival 51 studs off the beam: **thrown at 71 studs/s** to 97 away; the Wavebreaker hopped 11 studs onto its crest |
| 🔥 Nitro | A Skiff held on a 40-stud tow sat at 0 with the throttle down; Nitro **broke the chain** and it shot off to 130 |
| 📯 Rally Horn | The Cutter surged **102 → 153** and patched to full hull (406 → 420) |
| Bow gun | Real click at a rival 32 studs off the bow: the shot landed **within 0.1 studs of the aim**, 9 hull damage, the rival shoved away. A 5-keg chain reaction in Barrel Apocalypse from one shot (earlier in the session) |

![The Wavebreaker's Breaker: the rival Skiff thrown away in spray](2026-10-19-v13-2-breaker.jpg)

![HOOKED! Reeling in to board](2026-10-19-v13-2-hook-reel.jpg)

## 4. Controls (and the collision audit)

| Where | Keyboard / mouse | Controller | Touch |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| At the wheel | Click: **bow gun**. `Shift`: boost. `Space`: hop / super jump. `R`: the boat's ability on the water, a trick in the air. Hold `C`: drift. `E` or `X`: leave | `R2` gun, `X` boost, `A` hop, `R1` ability / trick, `B` drift, `Y` leave | GUN, BOOST, HOP, STUNT |
| On foot | Running builds speed. `Shift` or `C`: dash. `Space` twice: air jump. `F`: grapple (swing / pull / catch); hold `F` reels in; `F` or `Space` lets go. Click: sword | `B` dash, `A` jump, `L2` grapple | HOOK |

What was checked: at the wheel the click is the gun, never the sword (`Combat` refuses a driver's swing) and never the grapple (`F`); `R` was the anchor winch's key through V13 and is now only the ability/trick (the winch is gone: the anchor belongs to the Anchorjack); `Shift` on foot was sprint and is now the dash (no hold behaviour left to clash); a click over a button is the button's (`processed`); R2 at the wheel is bound above Roblox's own tool action. The controls card (`H`) says all of it. Not checked: a real controller, a real phone.

![The controls card in a raid](2026-10-19-v13-2-controls-card.jpg)

## 5. The skyship

`shared/SkyRoute.lua`, `server/Skyship.lua`, `Config.SKYSHIP`.

- **Seven routes** (the Westwind, the Eastwind, the Northern Arc, the Southern Sweep, the Spine, the Cinder Run, the Navy Run), each flown forwards or backwards, never the same as the raid before, chosen and shown when the Port opens. Each reaches 6 to 10 of the 16 major islands; every island is in reach on at least two routes (tested).
- **Finite reach**: the cannon throws at 215 (was 440): about **1,200 studs** from 540 up (was 3,560: the whole sea). Skull Rock from the middle of the sea is out of reach (tested).
- **The countdown is real**: aboard, the ship waits at its route's start for **10 s** with the cannons **locked by the server** (`Flight`/`Skyship` refuse a fire; the HUD says 🔒 SETS OFF). Aiming works. Then it flies the route in **32 s** (152 to 222 studs/s). Manual fire, the auto-fire of a map pick, the end-of-pass straggler fire and late joiners all go through the same check.
- **The six-minute clock starts when the pass ends** (42 s from boarding).
- **Picking on the map** (`M`) lights the islands in reach on this route; the ship fires you as it passes your pick's closest point. The map shows the route, the ship and the reach ring. Anyone still aboard at the end is fired at the best landing in reach.
- **Late joiners** board the ship mid-route (it flies back and forth, swinging round at the ends instead of jumping) and get 24 s on deck.
- **V12's dry landings, kept**: each route checks every island's landing spot by flying the actual throw from its closest pass (`Skyship.throwLands`), and moves it if needed. **All 110 route-and-island combinations come down dry within 22 studs of their spot.** Real flights in Studio landed 10 to 20 studs from the spot on seven islands (Crystal Isle 33, on a ledge above it).

![The route on the map: the Westwind, the ship at its start, the reach ring](2026-10-19-v13-2-route-map.jpg)

![🔒 SETS OFF: aboard and aiming, the cannons still locked](2026-10-19-v13-2-cannons-locked.jpg)

## 6. Going is a choice

`server/Raid.lua`, `shared/Lobby.lua`, client `PortHud.lua`, `Hud.lua`.

- The Port says **WAITING FOR RAIDERS** while nobody has joined: no countdown, no empty raid. **JOIN NEXT RAID** (or walking aboard the Little Goblin) signs you up; the first sign-up starts the 60 s countdown; once everyone signed up is aboard it leaves in 8 s. **SIGNED UP · STAY IN PORT** cancels. **AUTO-JOIN** signs you up for every raid until you turn it off.
- Only signed-up goblins go. Everyone else stays to shop, chat, watch (Spyglass), or JOIN a running raid late (while 2 minutes are left).
- **LEAVE THIS RAID** on the `H` card (two presses: "SURE? You lose this raid's gold. Press again") takes you home to the Port: what you carry drops for others, that raid's gold and Shinies are forfeited. If the last raider leaves, the raid ends.

Seen in Studio with real clicks: WAITING → JOIN (countdown 0:59, "1 signed up") → raid → skyship (route, prep) → fired onto Tide Vault → LEAVE, two presses → "FrikiEnriki sailed home to the Port", gold 0, raid over, the Port waiting again with the next chaos and route. Cancel and walk-aboard were checked earlier in the session.

## 7. World chaos

`server/WorldChaos.lua` (the server's events), `client/ChaosFx.lua` (all their visuals), rogue waves and whirlpools in the shared sea maths (`shared/Sea.lua`: the server and every driver's client float boats on the same water), `Config.CHAOS`.

Every raid draws **one** event (never the last raid's), shown in the Port with its icon and a line. During the six minutes it plays **episodes**: the first 22–34 s in, then one after another with 18–30 s of calm between, none in the last 18 s. Each is centred 80–260 studs off where goblins are (never on their heads, never within 650 of the Hoard, never in the Port), telegraphed, and drawn afresh (size, count, shape, place). Everything hits through the game's own rules: explosions are `Blast`s (creatures, sea mobs, the Navy, mines and kegs react), boats are shoved through `Boats.shove` with the crash grace (chaos batters, it never sinks), goblins through `Impact`'s grace (no juggling).

| Event | What happens | Seen in Studio |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ☄ Meteor Mayhem | 5–9 meteors (sometimes THE BIG ONE first, ×1.8) under burning rings; blasts throw boats up 120–170 and out, splash, set off kegs | A boat thrown high off the blast; crash grace stopped the landing from sinking it |
| 🐙 Kraken's Tantrum | 4–6 tentacles after bubbles: some sweep a 120° arc, some slam, some come up under a boat and toss it (190 up) | A Wavebreaker tossed 25 up, 320 → 298 hull |
| 🌊 Rogue Wave Rampage | 1–2 walls of water 20–30 high rolling at 58–74 across the sea; break against land | The sea rose 22.8 studs under a boat and **carried it 159 studs**, no damage |
| 💣 Cannonball Crossfire | An armada 520–650 off (always in deep water) shells a 180–250 zone for 14–18 s, sometimes rolling across the sea; 60% of shells aim at boats' paths | Rings and shells round the boat; armada ships placed in deep water after a beach spawn was fixed |
| 💥 Barrel Apocalypse | Fields of 26–40 kegs (70% powder) drift in; anything that goes bang sets off the ones near it, in chains | One bow-gun shot set off a 5-keg chain |
| 🌀 Whirlpool Outbreak | Wandering whirlpools (70–110 studs in radius) pull boats in, spin them round, fling them out of the far side | A boat spun at 70 studs/s and pulled to the eye |
| 👻 Haunted Seas | Twin portals (sail into one, out of the other) and phantom ships that ram | A boat in portal A came out at portal B |
| ⚡ Thunderstruck | The sky darkens, a crackling ring, then a giant strike on the busiest water: the shockwave throws boats and **SUPERCHARGES** them (a burst of speed), with chains of lightning between boats | 13 supercharges in one test, fastest throw 39 up |

After a raid: chaos cleared (`WorldChaos.reset`: no waves, whirlpools, barrels, portals or ships left), the next event and route chosen, opt-ins cleared (checked twice, two raids in a row).

![Rogue Wave Rampage](2026-10-19-v13-2-rogue-wave.jpg)

![Meteor Mayhem: a boat thrown off a blast](2026-10-19-v13-2-meteor-launch.jpg)

![Whirlpool Outbreak](2026-10-19-v13-2-whirlpools.jpg)

![Cannonball Crossfire](2026-10-19-v13-2-crossfire.jpg)

![Barrel Apocalypse and the bow gun](2026-10-19-v13-2-barrels-bow-gun.jpg)

![Haunted Seas: a ghost portal](2026-10-19-v13-2-ghost-portal.jpg)

![Thunderstruck: SUPERCHARGED](2026-10-19-v13-2-thunder-supercharged.jpg)

## 8. Performance

Each event forced in turn round the test goblin's Cutter with six AI boats circling it (Studio on the development PC, one client, Studio in front):

| Scene | Server frame (avg / worst) | Client fps |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Calm | 16.7 / 19.9 ms | 60–61 |
| Meteors | 16.7 / 19.1 ms | 60–61 |
| Kraken | 16.7 / 19.0 ms | 60–61 |
| Rogue waves | 16.7 / 20.2 ms | 60–61 |
| Crossfire | 16.7 / 19.9 ms | 60–61 |
| Barrels (31 kegs) | 16.7 / 19.6 ms | 60–61 |
| Whirlpools (4) | 16.7 / 19.3 ms | 60–61 |
| Haunted (3 ghost ships) | 16.7 / 19.7 ms | 60–61 |
| Thunder | 16.7 / 20.2 ms | 60–61 |
| **Barrels + meteors together** (27 kegs) | 16.7 / 19.9 ms | 60–61 |

The server never dropped below 60 steps a second; the client held 60 (it dipped to 36 for one second while the test boats spawned). Barrels are data, not physics parts (the server moves them and draws nothing; clients draw them); whirlpools and waves are maths in the shared sea; every visual is drawn on the clients (`ChaosFx`). **Not measured**: a full 3-player server, a phone.

## 9. Profile and economy

- **No profile migration needed**: boats are catalogue items (`boat_anchorjack` 500, `boat_wavebreaker` 550, `boat_corsair` 650 Shinies) owned the V11/V13 way, so every existing owner keeps everything. Free: Skiff and Cutter.
- **Robux**: inert product keys for the three new boats and the fleet bundle (now all eight), `id = nil`. A human creates any product in the Creator Dashboard (docs/MONETIZATION.md).
- `EconomySpec`: the whole fleet is still earnable in under 26 hours of ordinary raids.
- Pets: nothing depended on sprint. Spring Frog speeds the dash (kept), Shell Tortoise bounces a catch (now a thrown hook, still blocked), SPIRIT shortens a knockout.
- Leaving a raid forfeits that raid's gold and Shinies, so it can't be used to bank Shinies and skip the risk.

## 10. Tests and checks

- **107 Luau tests pass** in Studio (V13.1's 82, all kept, plus 25): `MovementSpec` (momentum: moving at once, the run, the top; a hard turn or stop spends it, a curve, jump or fall keeps it; swing speed kept in the air, sliding back after landing; the swing: swing or pull by height, a pendulum that never stretches the rope, pump, reel, release with a lift, a pull that arrives), `SkyRouteSpec` (finite reach; every route 6–10 islands, every island on 2+ routes; bounds and speed; the prep wait; the pass and the swing-round with no jump; reversed routes; in reach at the closest pass), `ChaosSpec` (eight events with names, icons, lines and tuning; several episodes with calm between; hits recoverable; the sea's chaos reaching clients intact; a rogue wave lifts, carries and breaks against land; a whirlpool swirls round and in), `BoatClassSpec` (ten classes in the showroom; no class better at everything; one speed band 105–120 and nobody much quicker to top speed; a 3,000-stud crossing from a standstill about the same for all; Nitro an escape, not a straight-line win; every ability escapes or disrupts; the bow gun shoves more than it hurts; snag, swing and hook become the right chains and a swing lets go as a sling), `LobbySpec` (a raid leaves only with somebody signed up and the countdown over; a raid nobody is left in ends).
- StyLua and Selene clean; `./scripts/check.ps1` (see the PR).
- Studio: everything in sections 2 to 8 above.

## 11. Bugs found and fixed while testing

| Found | Fix |
| --- | --- |
| The Corsair's boarding never happened: its own client says "arrived" alongside the rival, but the server sees that hull a moment late and the client saw the rival a moment late (27 studs apart at 94 and 68 studs/s) | On "arrived" the server allows both boats' speeds along the line × 0.35 s (`A.hook.lag`) |
| A boarded boat sped up (it was shoved along the line between the hulls: straight ahead when boarding from behind) | Shoved across the Corsair's heading |
| The bow gun's shots at something close went 15–20 studs long (every cannon's aim was floored at 6° down) | The bow gun may aim down to 40° (other cannons unchanged) |
| The skyship's auto-fire landed 59 studs off (the server's view of a goblin on the moving deck lags) | Throws from a fixed point on the ship; the client starts the flight there |
| The ship jumped back to the route's start after its pass | It swings round over 3 s and flies back |
| A meteor-thrown boat took big crash damage landing | Shoves give crash grace for their size |
| Kraken markers tinted the whole screen purple (a tall column) | Warning rings instead |
| Rogue waves weak near land, crests turned 90° | Softer shelter, crests along the front |
| Whirlpools orbited a boat forever | Stronger pull at the centre |
| The armada could spawn on a beach | Tries 16 headings for deep water |
| Leftover tentacle parts when not rendering | A cleanup backstop |
| The leave button covered "H closes this", and an old reset could relabel a second question early | Text moved left; the reset knows which question it belongs to |
| Frost Spire unreachable at its landing height on the Spine | Reach computed for the landing's height |

## 12. Not tested, or unverified

- **A second player**: boarding a real goblin (their treasure dropping), a snag or hook on a boat another client simulates (the tether is sent to that client: written, never seen), PvP with the bow gun, rally surging a friend, spectating and late entry with others.
- **Feel**: whether momentum's 2 s build feels good; whether the swing's 125 cap is too fast (it can fly you into trees); whether the compressed boats make the sea feel slower in a bad way; whether eight events are fun, too much or too little. **These are the playtest.**
- A real controller (R2 gun, L2 swing) and a phone (the GUN button).
- A full six-minute raid with three people under chaos; the events with every guardian (meteors were seen to throw creatures through `Blast`, not with each guardian).
- Pursuit interactions such as the Leviathan being hit by a meteor were not staged.
- The Spine route's Frost Spire landing passes in simulation; no real flight onto it was made.
- Studio's own mouse tool leaves the camera fixed; real mice do not (no game code sets it), but nobody has played a raid start with a real mouse since.

## 13. Playtest guide (for three people)

1. Everyone presses **Play**. You arrive in the Port. Look at the top left: **the next raid's chaos and the skyship's route**.
2. Press **JOIN NEXT RAID** (or walk up the gangplank). Try cancelling, and try AUTO-JOIN. Someone stays behind and watches from the Spyglass.
3. On the skyship: climb into a cannon (`E`) and aim. **It will not fire for 10 s.** Press `M`: the lit islands are in reach now; pick one, or fire yourself when your island comes into reach.
4. On foot: just run, and feel the speed build. Press `F` at a tree, a rock or a bridge above you and **swing**; `W` pumps, `F` or `Space` lets go. Try swinging onto a moving boat.
5. At sea: **click to fire the bow gun** at each other. Try every boat at least once (the Shipyard, or `P`): the Anchorjack's anchor on a friend's boat, the Corsair boarding a carrier, the Wavebreaker's ring in a crowd, the Skiff's Nitro to escape a chain.
6. Race home from a far island in different boats. Does any boat feel useless? Does anyone feel too slow?
7. Watch the chaos: is it funny? Too often? Too rare? Did it ever feel unfair?
8. Someone press `H` and **LEAVE THIS RAID** (twice) to check you go home.
9. Report what felt bad, what was funny, and send a screenshot of any red error.

## Report: 2026-10-18-v13-goblin-port.md

# V13: The Goblin Port (2026-10-18)

Requested with Ninety's "Loot Goblins — V13 One-Shot: The Goblin Port" brief, passed on by Enrik ("make me impressed, make me want to play it, make it reliable"). Built by Claude Opus 5.5 on 2026-10-18 on top of main after V11 and V12 merged.

**Read this first.** Everything below was built and tested by one AI on **one** Roblox Studio client on the development PC, through real key presses and clicks where it says so and through a Studio-only test hook (a Workspace script obeying a `DebugCmd` attribute, created in the Studio session and never committed) elsewhere. Nobody has played V13. It has never had a second player, a phone or a real controller; real DataStore saving and real Robux purchases have not run. Each claim below is labelled:

- **Tested**: implemented, and seen working in Studio or proven by a passing test.
- **Partly tested**: implemented; some paths seen, others only by rule or code reading.
- **Prototype**: works, but is a first version the team should judge.
- **Not implemented** / **Needs creator setup**.

## 1. Executive summary

V13 builds the half of Loot Goblins that happens between raids.

- **The Goblin Port** (Tested): a harbour town on its own island replaces the 10 s skyship intermission. A 60 s countdown, a boarding pier to a little airship (walking aboard is being ready; everyone aboard brings the raid forward to 8 s), a Shipyard with all seven boats on slipways, Mother Mossback's Menagerie with four pens of living pets, Madame Ragwort's Wardrobe, a Spyglass tower to watch the raid, and a winners' podium with a champion statue. Winners come home onto the podium; everyone else to the fountain.
- **Late entry and spectating** (Partly tested): join a running raid while two minutes or more are left; watch any raider with a camera and a bar. The server decides both. Seen with one goblin only.
- **Seven boat classes** (Tested in Studio, balance untested by people): the free Skiff and Cutter and five earned with Shinies (Reefhopper, Broadside, Stormrunner, Wraith, Ironbelly), each with its own silhouette, numbers, weakness and an ability on the stunt key. Every ability was fired through the real `R` key and accepted by the server.
- **The bestiary** (Tested): 37 new pets (42 in all) in four themes on one shared animator, each with a kind of movement and an idle quirk of its own; six shared utility archetypes so rarity is never power; seven island pets earned by escaping that island's creature.
- **Economy** (Tested by model and tests; pacing untested by people): deeds, ten achievements, profile v3 with an in-place v2 upgrade, a written model: a typical goblin earns a boat in about 2 to 4 hours, all five in about 14.
- **Monetization** (Needs creator setup): product keys for the boats and two show-only cosmetics, no ids, sales off.
- **A quiet raid screen** (Tested): icon moves with key chips, a slim stamina bar, a one-strip boat panel with the ability, a short objective chip that stops teaching after three raids.
- **A V11 bug found and fixed**: the server dropped the item from a shop request, so WEAR IT on anything already owned took that slot off.
- **76 Luau tests pass** (53 before; LobbySpec, BoatClassSpec and PetSpec are new). StyLua, Selene and both Rojo builds pass. 60 fps in the Port with the menagerie running.

## 2. Git branch, base and PR

- Branch `feature/v13-goblin-port`, from `origin/main` at `055953f` ("Merge pull request #23 from EnrikR2002/feature/v12-cohesion-pass"), which already contains V11 (PR #22) and V12 (PR #23). That is the verified correct base: V13 depends on both.
- PR [#24](https://github.com/EnrikR2002/Loot-Goblins/pull/24) against `main`. **Not merged** (the brief: "Do not merge any PR").
- Shared-notebook lessons from this work: [Roblox-Team-Knowledge PR #11](https://github.com/EnrikR2002/Roblox-Team-Knowledge/pull/11) (pending when this was written).

## 3. Lobby architecture

| Piece | Where | What |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The rules | `src/shared/Lobby.lua` (pure, tested) | `inPort(position)`, `raidLeft`, `canJoinLate(phase, now, endsAt, alreadyIn)`, `portEndsAt(now, endsAt, inPort, ready, inServer)`, `raidAbandoned`, `sortTargets`/`cycle` (the spectating ring), `status` (what the Port screen says) |
| The round | `src/server/Raid.lua` (rewritten) | phases `port` and `raid`; an explicit `participants` set; `start` (everyone in the server goes), `joinLate`, `finish` (results and Shinies for participants only, everyone home, winners to the podium), `placeCharacter` (every spawn: aboard, Goblin Cove or the Port), the readiness sweep every 0.25 s |
| The town | `src/server/Port.lua` (new, ~1,500 lines) | builds the island and every building; `arrive`, `arriveWinners`, `isReady`, `setChampion`, spectating (`spectate`, `targets`, `tick`, `stopAll`) |
| Isolation | `Lobby.inPort` asked by `Combat`, `Kegs`, `Poltergoblin`, `Recall`, `Storms`, `Tornadoes`, `Blast.safe` | nothing of a raid reaches the Port |
| The screens | client `PortHud.lua`, `Spectate.lua`, `PortLife.lua` | the Port's sign and wallet, the departures board, fades; the spectator camera and bar; the menagerie's pets |

State the client reads: workspace `RaidPhase` (`port`/`raid`), `PhaseEndsAt`, `RaidClockAt`, `PortReady`, `PortCount`; player `Zone`, `InRaid`, `Ready`, `Spectating`. Server authority is complete: the client only asks (`PortRequest("join")`, `PortRequest("spectate", action)`, rate-limited to five a second).

## 4. Port environment (Tested)

![The Port from above](2026-10-18-v13-port-aerial.jpg)

Built at start-up from parts and terrain, about 1,080 parts in `PortTown` (streamed) and 35 in `PortCore` (persistent: floors, gangplank, podium, boards). At `Config.PORT.CENTER` (0, 0, 4600), more than 1,500 studs beyond its own radius from every island (a test checks it), out of the raid's streaming range.

- **Plaza**: cobbled disc, the Golden Goblin fountain, two bounce pads, lamps, bunting, market stalls, arrival rings facing the pier.
- **Boarding pier → The Little Goblin**: a pier, a platform, a gangplank and a little airship; its deck is the ready zone. A departures board at the pier's start shows the countdown (or the raid's time left), written by each client. A gold marker floats over the gangplank until you are aboard.
- **Shipyard** (west): seven slipways, each boat on chocks with a board (name, role) and a prompt that opens the showroom on it.
- **Mother Mossback's Menagerie** (east): a pavilion with its keeper and four themed pens where up to ten pets each wander (section 15).
- **Madame Ragwort's Wardrobe** (south): a red-roofed shop with three dressed mannequins in the window.
- **The Spyglass** (north-east): a tower with a telescope and benches; its prompt starts spectating.
- **The Podium** (south-west): three steps for the winners, a champion plinth with a dressed statue and a crown, and a banner with their name and gold.

![The sign, the departures board and the Port card](2026-10-18-v13-port-sign-and-help.jpg)

## 5. Round lifecycle and timings (Tested)

| Phase | Length | What happens |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Port | `PORT.DURATION` 60 s | arrive, shop, watch, ready up. Everyone aboard: brought forward to `READY_SECONDS` 8 s (never pushed back). Empty server: held |
| Launch window | `SKYSHIP.WINDOW` 20 s | everyone in the server boards the skyship and fires off (unchanged V9 to V12 flow) |
| Raid | `RAID_DURATION` 360 s | the clock starts when the window closes; final rush and last call unchanged |
| Results | in the Port | everyone in the raid arrives home (winners on the podium), the results card shows for 22 s, the champion dances after 2.7 s |

About 440 s a cycle, 8.2 raids an hour. Seen in Studio: the countdown; walking aboard took it from 571 s to 6 s ("Everyone's aboard! Casting off in 6..."); the raid starting by itself and launching the goblin; raid end with podium, statue, results card and payout; a raid whose only raider left ending at once.

![Everyone aboard](2026-10-18-v13-ready-all-aboard.jpg)

## 6. Late-entry policy (Partly tested)

A goblin in the Port may join a raid that has at least `LATE_JOIN_MIN` (120 s) left: the JOIN button on the Port's sign, the JOIN button on the spectator bar, or the prompt at the pier (enabled only while allowed). They board the skyship like everyone else (with its deck grace), start with **zero gold**, and their participation is counted from when they joined (Shinies are earned by participation, not by being in the server). Too late: "Too little of this raid is left. Get ready for the next one!" A goblin who joins the server mid-raid arrives in the Port and can watch or join.

Tested by `LobbySpec` (plenty left, too little, no raid, already in, junk times) and by the Port screen showing "Too late to join: watch it" with under two minutes left. **Not seen**: an actual late join while someone else raids (with one client, the only raider leaving ends the raid).

## 7. Spectator implementation (Partly tested)

- **Server** (`Port.spectate`): only a non-participant may watch, only a participant alive in the raid may be watched, the target is chosen from a ring sorted by name (`Lobby.cycle`), the server streams the world round the target (`ReplicationFocus`, `RequestStreamAroundAsync`) and follows them every 0.5 s, moves the spectator on when the target is gone (`SpectateSwitch`), and stops everyone when the raid ends or the spectator joins (`SpectateEnd(why)`).
- **Client** (`Spectate.lua`): camera on the target's humanoid, the goblin's controls off and its movement keys caught, a bar (◀ name ▶, gold and what they are doing, the raid clock, JOIN while allowed, PORT), keys Left/Right (Q/E, D-pad, L1/R1) and Backspace (B). A respawn while watching keeps watching; leaving restores camera and controls.

Seen: with the watch state forced onto the only goblin, the bar, the clock and the Port screen stepping aside; W moved the goblin 34 studs in the first version (controls alone were not enough), **0 studs** after the movement keys were also caught; Backspace ended it and W walked again (28 studs). Refusals seen: watching with no raid running. **Not seen**: watching another player, switching targets, a target dying or leaving, streaming round a far raider.

![Spectating (the account name is blurred)](2026-10-18-v13-spectate.jpg)

## 9. Free boat balance (Prototype)

- **Skiff** keeps its V7 to V12 numbers (135 top speed, 160 hull) and gains NITRO, so the free starter boat is the best escape boat in a straight line.
- **Cutter** was the slow one; V13 raised it a little so it does not feel like a barge (accel 68 → 72, top 104 → 110, turn 1.7 → 1.8) and gave its driver a BOW GUN on the stunt key. It now just outruns a patrol ship (106) and carries three friends.
- Neither free boat is dominated by any paid one (the balance test in section 11).

## 10. Specialty boat designs (Prototype, abilities Tested)

- **Reefhopper** (350, stunt boat): small, light, twin pontoons and a gold spring. Jumps 25% higher, steers well in the air (0.75 air control), tricks 35% faster and lands with a bigger burst. SPRING leaps off flat water; Space in the air hops once more. Weak: 150 hull, a little slower on the straight.
- **Broadside** (700, gunboat): a big square-rigged warship. BROADSIDE fires three shots from the side you look at; two passenger seats are gunners on side cannons. Weak: slow (98), wide-turning (1.45), a big target, a 6 s boost cooldown.
- **Stormrunner** (550, storm chaser): one tall lightning sail and a spinning vane. 18% faster in a storm cell or near a tornado, thrown 45% farther when it bails out of a funnel, and TWISTER spins up a real tornado 85 studs behind that drifts after it for 12 s (at most four summoned on the sea; never near home or in the Port). Weak: ordinary in calm water; its own twister catches it if it stops for long after a 5 s grace.
- **Wraith** (500, phantom): low, narrow, black, translucent glowing sails. The sharpest steering (3.1) and highest grip; PHANTOM slips it sideways and leaves a ghost running on that fools pursuers within 700 studs for 2.6 s. Weak: the most fragile hull (120, crashes hurt 25% more).
- **Ironbelly** (600, bruiser): a riveted iron tug with a ram, tyres and a funnel. 640 hull taking 30% crash damage, shoved half as far, rights itself 60% faster, four passengers, swimmers can climb aboard from 40 studs. RAM PLOW is a 2.6 s charge that shoves boats aside once each and knocks pursuers back. Weak: the slowest and widest-turning (96, 1.35).

## 12. Mounted cannon and ability systems (Tested)

How one press works: `R` (R1, touch STUNT) → `BoatDrive.stunt` → in the air a trick, on the water `BoatSim` plays the physical part at once and reports `out.ability` → the client sends `BoatAbilityRequest(aimPoint)` → `BoatAbilities.request` checks the driver, a 0.2 s rate limit and its own cooldown (`AbilityReadyAt`, with 0.25 s slack), fires whatever the server owns, widens `Boats.police`'s allowance for that boat for the burst, and broadcasts a `BoatFx` for everyone's effects; a refusal sends `AbilityRefused` and the client forgets its prediction. If the server is simulating the hull, the ability is queued into its own BoatSim step.

- **Cannons**: the Cutter's bow gun fires within a 70° cone up to 420 studs where the driver looks; the Broadside's volley picks the side by the aim and fires three staggered shots 9 studs apart up to 300 studs. Both use `Config.BOAT_SHOT` (radius 13, 6 damage, 70 knockback, 22 hull, 82 boat push): built to shove and splash, not to sink. Boat guns cannot hurt anyone inside the home ward or in the Port; a shot never hits its own boat. The Broadside's two gunner seats sit by side cannons with a 3.4 s cooldown and an arc check (a side gun cannot fire across the deck).
- **Twister**: `Tornadoes.summon` (owner, life 12 s, drift 12 studs/s along the boat's heading, at most four summoned, one per owner), refused over shallow water, near the Hoard or in the Port.
- **Phantom**: a ghost model runs on for 2.6 s; `Pursuit.decoy` makes pursuers within 700 studs chase it (no lock-on tell while fooled); the Leviathan and Ghost Fleet are fooled too.
- **Ram Plow**: a 2.6 s charge (thrust ×1.7, top speed ×1.18, shoves taken ×0.2); a boat within 10 studs of the bow is shoved once at 95 studs/s; pursuers in front are knocked back (`Pursuit.shoveAt`).

Seen through the real `R` key in Studio, each accepted by the server (its `AbilityReadyAt` set): Wraith PHANTOM (ghost afterimage, 11 s cooldown), Stormrunner TWISTER (feed "…whipped up a tornado!"), Reefhopper SPRING, Broadside BROADSIDE (three shots in flight), Ironbelly RAM PLOW, Cutter BOW GUN, Skiff NITRO (215 studs/s; a second press showed "NITRO 14s"). In the air (a storm funnel) the same key did a trick ("SPIN CYCLE"), as intended.

## 15. Pet animations and personalities (Tested)

One animator for every pet (`PetLook.pose`): parts in named groups (legs, wings, fins, tails, chains of segments, tentacles, arms, head, lid, halo, orbit, flame, lure, bell, puff) and a species row with its **kind** (walker, hopper, plodder, crawler, roller; flier, floater, swimmer, slither) and **quirk**. Walkers stride, hoppers hop, plodders stomp, the coin rolls on its edge, swimmers beat their tails in the air, slitherers wave down their segments, floaters drift. Quirks play when the goblin stands still (an ink cloud, bubbles, spores, sparks from Fuse's fuse); a few answer the game (the pufferfish puffs up while something big chases its goblin, the penguin belly-slides at a run, Peek freezes whenever the camera can see it and catches up when it cannot). Followers ride decks, cling on in the air and water, and keep station at any speed (V11's rules, by kind). The shop preview and the Port's pens use the same animator; the pens' pets wander, look at a goblin who comes near, skip out of the way, and the nearest shows its name and price (✔ when owned, 🏆 for a trophy).

`PetSpec` builds every species, checks no two look identical, and poses each through 61 frames in four situations including its quirk with every part staying near its origin.

## 17. Pet collection progression (Prototype)

34 pets for Shinies (◆70 to ◆550, 6,260 in all), seven escape trophies, one premium show pet. The early buys are cheap (four under ◆100); the island pets are the long-term aspiration and each one is a story ("I outran the Leviathan"). The pens let a goblin see every pet before buying. One pet out at a time; pets change only in the Port or at the Hoard.

## 18. Economy modelling (Tested by model)

One currency, Shinies. Raid payout (`Economy.payout`): participation 8, +1 per gold banked up to 22, +15 for a win, +3 for an underdog bank (banked something, finished in the bottom half), and **deeds** once a raid each: steal from a spot 2, escape (a pursuer gives up at the sanctuary) 4, snatch from a downed goblin 3, clean tricks 1 each up to 3; capped at 50. Assumption: 8.2 raids an hour (60 s Port + 20 s launch + 360 s raid; less if the Port is cut short by everyone readying).

## 21. Progression and achievements (Tested)

Ten new achievements (21 in all): **Light Fingers** (first steal, 20), seven escape trophies that each grant that island's pet (**Serpent's Friend** Little Leviathan 60, **Sun Dodger** Sunny 60, **Echo Chamber** Little Echo 40, **Wool Over Their Eyes** Lambkin 40, **Ghost Runner** Bones 60, **Live Wire** Zap 40, **Don't Blink** Peek 40), **The Great Escape** (ten escapes, 80) and **Fleet Admiral** (bank treasure having come home in four classes of boat, 100). ## 22. Monetization options (Needs creator setup)

Product keys in `Config.MONETIZATION.PRODUCTS`, all `id = nil`: a pass for each unlockable boat (also earnable), the Gilded Whelp (show pet, no ability), the Moon Jelly look, and `bundle_fleet` (all five boats; no shop item points at it yet). `SALES_ENABLED = false`. No product id or Robux price was invented. docs/MONETIZATION.md has the team's decision notes.

## 23. Creator configuration requirements

A teammate creates each game pass or developer product in the Creator Dashboard, chooses its price, and gives the AI the id; the AI fills `id` and turns `SALES_ENABLED` on when the team says so; then a published test place with API access for test purchases (docs/MONETIZATION.md, "Turning one on" and "Testing safely").

## 24. Profile schema changes and migration (Tested by spec; live store not run)

`ProfileSchema.VERSION` 3. New stats `steals`, `escapes`; new maps `escapedFrom` (island → count) and `classBanks` (boat class → count); `equipped.boat`. A v2 profile loads as "upgraded" (`migratedFrom = 2`): everything kept, new stats zero, saved as v3 at once; a V7 profile still migrates; a newer version is never opened or written (a v2 server will not overwrite a v3 profile). `PersistenceSpec` covers the v2 upgrade field by field.

## 25. Purchase and receipt safety (unchanged; Tested by spec)

V11's server-only grants, idempotent receipts and pass checks are unchanged (`ReceiptsSpec` passes). New items go through the same `grants` table. Buying with Shinies is charged once under rapid repeats (EconomySpec), and the server alone decides prices and ownership.

## 26. Multiplayer replication (Partly tested)

Everything a second player sees comes from server state and attributes: who is in the raid, ready, spectating; boat classes (`BoatType`), abilities (`BoatFx` "ability" broadcast to everyone for effects; shots, tornadoes and decoys are server objects); pets from `Pet` and `Look`; the champion statue on the server. **Not seen with a second player**: another goblin's pet, ability effects on someone else's screen, two goblins readying, a crowd in the Port.

## 31. Bugs discovered and fixed (this session)

1. **V11 bug, fixed**: `Main.server.lua` passed only the first argument of a `ShopRequest` to `Progress.handle`, so "equip, slot, item" arrived as "equip, slot": WEAR IT / BRING OUT / SAIL IT on anything already owned **took that slot off**, and outfit names were dropped. Only a purchase (which wears the item itself) ever changed a look. Found when the parrot would not come out at the Hoard; confirmed by reading the profile through the test hook.
2. After buying a pet the wardrobe's stage showed the Crab (the try-on was cleared and the stage fell back to what was worn); the chosen pet or boat now stays on the stage.
3. The airship's 20-stud neon ready ring bloomed into a blinding yellow deck; it is painted now.
4. The sea compass sat behind the Port's sign; hidden in the Port.
5. The sign's line was cut off; widened and shortened.
6. Long feed lines were cut off; they wrap.
7. 🪝, 🤾 and 🪙 render as boxes in Roblox's font; replaced by 🎣, 🏈 and COINS.
8. The Port help card's rows shrank unevenly; fixed size.
9. While spectating, turning the controls off alone let the goblin walk away; the movement keys are now caught too.
10. A Stormrunner that had slowed down was swallowed by its own new twister; its boat now ignores funnels for 5 s after summoning.
11. The results card still mentioned the old cannon bell; it says "walk aboard the Little Goblin" and lists deeds.
12. Lint: a duplicated branch in `Boats.displayModel`, an unused variable.

## 32. Remaining limitations

- One client: no second player, so spectating others, late entry beside other raiders, crowds in the Port and abilities against people are unseen (section 26).
- Studio's simulated keys cannot hold a ProximityPrompt; the Port's counters and the pier prompt were reached by `P` and test commands, not by holding E (their code is the same prompt path V11 used for the tailor's stall).
- Balance, prices, the 60 s Port and the deed values are first guesses with a model, not measurements of fun.
- The Stormrunner's own twister can catch it after the grace if it stops: by design a ride, untested by people.
- From high up, the Port's water meets the far-sea plane in a straight seam. The champion statue is a plain mannequin. A large part of the Port's island south of the buildings is empty grass.
- The showroom's stat card covers the lower part of the boat preview.
- Dash, drift, sprint, keg and Poltergoblin still have no touch buttons.
- No real controller, phone, live DataStore or purchase.

## 33. Deferred work

- A real two-to-four-player playtest (the guide below), then tune the Port's length, the prices and the deeds from it.
- Spectating polish once two players can try it (a free camera, a mini-scoreboard of the raiders).
- Showing the `bundle_fleet` pass in the shop if the team decides to sell it.
- Filling the empty south of the Port (a practice slipway to try boats in? a race track?), if the team likes the town.
- Touch buttons for the remaining moves; a phone check of the new HUD.

## 34. Human acceptance questions

- Is 60 seconds in the Port right? Does walking aboard to get ready make sense without being told?
- Do the seven boats feel genuinely different? Which become favourites, and is any obviously too weak or too strong? Are the cannons fun to fire and fair to be hit by?
- Are the new pets appealing? Too alike? Do they keep up and stay out of the camera?
- Does the raid screen feel cleaner, and is anything important now missing?
- Does V13 make you want to come back for the next boat, or does it distract from the raid?

## Human playtest guide

**Setup**: double-click **Play Loot Goblins**, then in Studio **Test tab > Server & Clients > 3 players > Play** (or one player with the blue Play button). You arrive in the Port.

**The Port (5 minutes)**
1. Walk around. Can you tell where to buy boats, pets and clothes without being told? Press `H` for the Port card.
2. Walk to the Shipyard; press `E` at a boat. Look at its stats. Try the pet pens: stand next to pets and read their names.
3. Everyone walk up the gangplank onto the little airship. Does the countdown drop to 8? Was that clear?

**Boats (one or two raids)**
4. Use the free Skiff and Cutter first: on the water press `R` (controller R1). Then buy a boat (the test server gives no free Shinies: earn some, or ask the AI to give the test goblins Shinies), choose it with SAIL IT in the Port, and press `B` in a raid to call it.
5. Try each class's ability. Which feels best? Is the Broadside's volley or the bow gun annoying to be hit by? Does the Ironbelly's ram feel mighty? Does the Wraith's ghost fool a pursuer?

**Watching and joining**
6. One player stays in the Port while the others raid: press WATCH. Do left/right change who you watch? Is it fun? Press JOIN with more than two minutes left: do you get on the skyship?

**Pets and progression**
7. Buy a cheap pet and take it on a raid. Does it keep up? Does it get in the way?
8. After a raid: is the results card clear? Is there something you want to save for?

**Tell the AI**: what felt bad, what you would change, and send a screenshot of any red error in the Output window.

## Report: 2026-10-18-v13-1-playtest-fixes.md

# V13.1: the V13 playtest fixes (2026-10-18)

Ninety played V13 (the Goblin Port) and sent ten points to fix ("go, make me impressed"). Built by Claude Opus 5.5 on branch `fix/v13-playtest-feedback`, stacked on V13 (`feature/v13-goblin-port`, PR #24, not merged), in one session.

**Read this first.** Everything below was built and tested by one AI on **one** Roblox Studio client, through a Studio-only test hook (a Workspace script obeying a `DebugCmd` attribute; never committed) and real key presses where it says so. Nobody has played V13.1. It has never had a second player.

![KNOCKED OUT! you dropped your treasure, up in 5](2026-10-18-v13-1-knocked-out.jpg)

## The ten points, and what happens now

| # | Ninety's point | What changed | Seen in Studio |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | The Ghost Fleet gets stuck and doesn't follow; it should follow alongside the pirates | Ships and dinghies sail **through land** (ghosts); ships surge to 330 and rise again behind a thief they lost; once the pirates are in the dinghies the ships **escort** them on both sides instead of sinking | A 40 s run from 700 studs off Skull Rock: ships 145 to 200 studs off the whole time, dinghies 10 to 60; the thief knocked out at 24 s by pirates and shells |
| 2 | The Guardian's hit on a boat should send it flying very high and spinning | Thrown 255 studs/s up (**about 170 studs**) and **tumbling end over end** for the whole flight (a new BoatSim "tumble" that lands level); the boat police allow the altitude | 170 studs up, two launches in 32 s, the boat upside down mid-flight; a second run's launches knocked the carrier out |
| 3 | No boss steals treasure; treasure drops only at death; death is a 5 s knockout, no respawn; all bosses attack a carrier repeatedly and reliably | **The knockout** (`server/Knockout.lua`): health 0 is 5 s down where you fell, treasure dropped there, up with full health; no world hit ever takes treasure (`Loot.knockLoose` hurts a carrier instead: 22 per hit, about four knock them out); every creature strike on a carrier counts; pursuers wait by a knocked-out thief | See the table below |
| 4 | Jade frogs: attack on the island and hop into the water reliably | Tangle Isle's imps became **three jade frogs**: they bound after a carrier and **pounce** (a ring, then a belly slam); the moment the thief is in the water they hop in after them, as a pack bounding over the waves that pounces on a ringed boat | On land: a hit every 2 to 3 s, a still goblin knocked out in 16 s. At sea: out 0.2 s after the thief reached the water, entering 59 studs away on the thief's side; a still boat knocked out in 13 s |
| 5 | The Aurora Gem island boss and its chase into the water need a rework | **The Chill** chases a carrier anywhere on Frost Spire and drops **hail** (a ring, then ice) every 3.4 s; at sea it comes down after the thief at once and bursts **ice spikes** up under a ringed boat | On land: hail hit every 3 to 5 s. At sea: out 0.2 s after the thief reached the water, the island Chill hidden meanwhile; three ice-spike hits in 15 s on a boat sailing straight (ring, strike, rest, chase, every 7 to 8 s) |
| 6 | The Leviathan needs to attack | Its lunge **bites**: a 0.9 s roar with jaws open, then 150 faster than the boat for 1.2 s; a boat holding its course is caught and thrown end over end | Four bites in 30 s on a boat sailing straight through deep water |
| 7 | Pick treasure up by boating over it | `Loot.sweepBoats`: a driver with empty hands whose hull passes over loose treasure takes it | Picked up the floating Crystal Heart 1.6 s after setting off toward it, still seated |

| 9 | Sunset Poltergoblin, keep the code, free E | `Config.POLTER_ENABLED = false`: the server ignores the request; E and Y no longer cast it; its slot and card lines are gone; a step short of a prompt still says "A step closer" | E and Y pressed on foot: no spirit |
| 10 | Calling a boat: keep the tesla arrival, stop reliably near you; make B readable at the edge with treasure | The boat races in (188 studs/s) and **brakes hard to a dead stop** at the water nearest you (followed as you walk the shore), then **holds** there 30 s; a big gold pulsing **B · CALL A BOAT** for a carrier at the island's edge, then **A BOAT IN 12s**, **YOUR BOAT IS COMING**, **YOUR BOAT IS HERE · E TO CLIMB IN** | Stopped from 188 studs/s in under a second and held still 6 s; parked where the sand flat drops to skiff depth |

![LAUNCHED BY THE GUARDIAN: the skiff tumbling high over the sea, the danger arrow naming the Guardian's speedboat](2026-10-18-v13-1-guardian-launch.jpg)

![B · CALL A BOAT at the shore with treasure](2026-10-18-v13-1-shore-hint.jpg)

![The called boat parked off the beach, its green beam up: YOUR BOAT IS HERE · E TO CLIMB IN](2026-10-18-v13-1-boat-parked.jpg)

## The knockout in detail (point 3)

- The humanoid's Dead state is switched off on the server and on the goblin's own client (the client runs its own humanoid's states), so health 0 is just a number; `Knockout.watch` turns it into a knockout. Roblox's own health regeneration is held back while they are down.
- Down: flat on the back on foot (their own client lays the body down), slumped at the wheel in a boat (the boat coasts; BoatDrive ignores their keys). The screen dims, **KNOCKED OUT!** wobbles, and it counts down and says who did it. Nothing targets them (`Util.aliveRoot`), and their pursuer, the Ghost Fleet and the Leviathan wait 9 s by them and their treasure.
- The treasure drops where they lie, loose: a rival can take it, and they can grab it back when they get up (the chase resumes).
- Up: full health, where they were, 2 s before the world can hit them again.
- Respawns left: a body that falls out of the world, and the Reset button (for a goblin who is stuck); both drop the treasure first.
- Feed: "… was KNOCKED OUT and dropped the …" (or, empty-handed, "… was knocked out by …").

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Health drained to 0 while carrying | Knocked out, treasure loose, same place; up after 5 s with 100 health, not platform-standing |
| Creature hits on a carrier | No drop; 22 health each after the grab's brief immunity; a Watcher finished the knockout on its own between test calls |
| Knocked out at the wheel | Stayed seated (a first version unseated the driver: a "stand up" helper for grapple catches used `ChangeState(GettingUp)`; replaced by a quiet cancel), treasure loose, driving again after 5 s |
| Pursuer during the knockout | The jade frogs circled and the chase continued |
| Ghost Fleet during a knockout | Gave up after 3 s in the first run; now waits 9 s like the others |

## Design decisions

- **A carrier hit is 22 on top of the creature's own damage**, so four or five hits knock a carrier out; a player who dodges rings will take far fewer. Non-carriers keep V8's gentler rules (scaled damage, no one-hit knockout).
- **Grace stays**: one world hit per 1.2 s, so creatures attack repeatedly but never juggle.
- **The frogs and the Chill set out from where their island creature is, on the thief's side**, and the island creature hides while its sea form is out: one creature, not two.
- **Ghost ships phase through land** rather than steering round it: ghosts that cannot be wedged is the simplest reliable answer and fits them.
- **The called boat parks where the water is deep enough for it**, which off a long sand flat can be 60 studs out; it holds there rather than drifting off.
- **SPIRIT pets** (they sped up Poltergoblin) now shorten the knockout, so nobody's pet lost its use.
- **Rivals still steal** (sword, keg, cannon, grapple catch): the point was "no bosses steal".

![A jade frog pounce: the green ring under the goblin](2026-10-18-v13-1-jade-frog-pounce.jpg)

![At sea with the Jade Frog: the danger arrow names THE JADE FROGS](2026-10-18-v13-1-jade-frogs-at-sea.jpg)

## Tests and checks

- **82 Luau tests pass** in Studio (V13's 76, plus `PlaytestSpec`: the knockout's numbers, Poltergoblin off, the Guardian's height and the tumble landing level and passing upside down, a tumble starting from the water and paying nothing, the Leviathan's lunge able to close to a bite, the called boat's stopping distance).
- StyLua and Selene clean; `./scripts/check.ps1` passes (see the PR).
- Server heartbeat 0.42 ms at 60 physics frames a second mid-raid. The client read 60 fps earlier in the session with Studio in front; a later reading of 15 was Studio's background cap.

## Not tested

- A second player: a rival taking a knocked-out goblin's treasure, two goblins in one fight.
- The Reset button's respawn; a knockout in lava (it can repeat after the 2 s grace); the Guardian throwing heavy classes; a phone or a real controller.
- The creature numbers are first guesses: the knockout times above are for a goblin who stood still or sailed straight.

## Playtest guide

1. Double-click **Play Loot Goblins**, press the blue **Play** button, walk aboard the airship, fly to an island.
2. **Tangle Isle** (the Jade Frog): steal it and run. The frogs bound after you: step off the green rings. Jump in the sea: they hop in after you.
3. **Frost Spire** (the Aurora Gem): the Chill rains hail on you; at sea it bursts ice spikes under you.
4. **Sun Temple** (the Golden Idol): take it to sea and get punched sky high by the Guardian's fist.
5. **Skull Rock** (the Chalice): the ghost ships should stay with you all the way, beside their dinghies.
6. Get **knocked out** (let something keep hitting you): 5 s down, the treasure on the ground, then up again. Grab it back.
7. Drop a treasure in the sea (Q from a boat) and **drive over it**.
8. In a boat, press **E** to get out. On foot with nothing near, E does nothing now.
9. With treasure at the edge of an island: the big **B · CALL A BOAT**. Press B, and watch it race in and stop beside you.
10. Tell the AI what felt bad, especially whether the bosses now hit too hard or not hard enough.
